soils.name: Airy houseplant mix
soils.short: good universal potting mix with extra perlite
soils.note: Squeeze a handful when moist: it should hold together and then crumble.

soils.name: Chunky aroid mix
soils.short: chunky aroid mix (bark, perlite, coco coir)
soils.note: Their roots climb trees in the wild, so they want air as much as water.

soils.name: Gritty succulent mix
soils.note: Water should run straight through. If the mix stays dark for more than a few days, add more grit.

soils.name: Orchid bark mix
soils.note: Air-loving roots: no ordinary compost at all.

soils.name: Ericaceous mix
soils.note: Buy bags labelled ericaceous or lime-free, and water with rainwater where you can.

soils.name: Citrus mix
soils.note: Free-draining but rich, slightly acidic.

soils.name: Veg and herb compost
soils.note: Rich and moisture-holding, for hungry fast growers.

soils.name: Moisture-keeping mix
soils.note: Stays evenly damp without going soggy.

soils.name: Mediterranean mix
soils.note: Lean and sunny: rich compost makes them soft and short-lived.

soils.name: African violet mix
soils.note: Very light and fluffy so fine roots can spread.

soils.name: Carnivorous plant mix
soils.short: carnivorous plant mix (sphagnum peat and sand, no fertilizer)
soils.note: Nutrient-free on purpose. Rainwater or distilled water only.

soils.name: No soil
soils.short: no soil at all (mounted or loose)
soils.note: They drink through their leaves.

soils.name: Clay garden soil
soils.forGroups: Roses, fruit trees, hardy perennials in the ground
soils.note: Rich but sticky. Add compost and grit; never use it alone in pots.

soils.name: Sandy soil
soils.note: Warms fast but dries fast and loses food. Mulch and feed more often.

soils.name: Loam
soils.note: The easy one: holds moisture and still drains.

soils.name: Peaty soil
soils.note: Acid and moisture-holding. Hard to re-wet once dry.

soils.name: Chalky soil
soils.note: Stony and alkaline. Acid lovers turn yellow here.

soils.name: Silty soil
soils.note: Fertile, but crusts on top. Mulch and avoid walking on it wet.

soils.name: Volcanic soil
soils.note: Airy and mineral-rich. Holds food well.

soils.name: Pumice mix
soils.note: Feed lightly but often, as pumice holds little food.

soils.name: Akadama bonsai mix
soils.note: Akadama softens over 2 to 3 years; repot then.

soils.name: Kanuma azalea mix
soils.note: Turns pale when dry, darker when wet.

soils.name: Coco coir mix
soils.note: Rinse coir to remove salt. It holds little food, so feed regularly.

soils.name: LECA (semi-hydro)
soils.note: Keep a small water reservoir and use hydro nutrients.

soils.name: Sphagnum moss
soils.note: Repack loosely. Replace once it turns slimy.

soils.name: Coarse bark mix
soils.note: Dries fast. Water more often in summer.

soils.name: Fine bark mix
soils.note: Airy yet moist. Good for fine-rooted epiphytes.

soils.name: Mineral cactus mix
soils.note: Almost no rot risk. Water deeply, then wait.

soils.name: Lithops mix
soils.short: very gritty mix for living stones
soils.note: Water only when they're actively growing.

soils.name: Seed sowing mix
soils.note: Fine and low in food so roots search.

soils.name: Cutting mix
soils.note: Airy and clean. Pot on once roots form.

soils.name: Herb mix
soils.note: Lean and sharp. Rich soil makes weak, bland herbs.

soils.name: Tomato container mix
soils.note: Hungry crops: feed weekly once fruits set.

soils.name: Raised bed mix
soils.note: Top up with compost each spring.

soils.name: Aquatic soil
soils.note: Heavy so it stays put underwater. No compost: it fouls water.

soils.name: Bog mix
soils.note: Keep wet with rainwater. No feed, no tap water.

soils.name: Terrarium mix
soils.note: Airy and clean so it doesn't sour.

soils.name: Palm mix
soils.note: Free draining with some weight for tall plants.

soils.name: Bromeliad mix
soils.note: Loose and airy. Water also into the cup.

soils.name: Hoya mix
soils.note: Chunky and airy; let it dry between waterings.

soils.name: Begonia mix
soils.note: Light and moist but never soggy.

soils.name: Fruit tree pot mix
soils.note: Weight keeps tall trees steady in wind.

soils.name: Rice hull mix
soils.note: A greener perlite swap.

components.name: Perlite
components.note: Puffed volcanic glass. Light, doesn't break down, keeps roots breathing.

components.name: Pumice
components.note: Porous volcanic stone. Heavier than perlite, so it stays mixed in and steadies tall pots.

components.name: Orchid bark
components.note: Fir or pine bark pieces. Big gaps for air, slowly breaks down over 1–2 years.

components.name: Coco coir
components.note: Coconut husk fibre. A peat-free sponge that rewets easily. Rinse salty brands first.

components.name: Peat-free compost
components.note: Wood fibre, green compost and coir. Holds moisture and some food; kinder to bogs.

components.name: Sphagnum peat
components.note: Only for plants that truly need it, like carnivorous plants. Use sparingly.

components.name: Sphagnum moss
components.note: Living or dried moss. Great for rooting cuttings and orchids.

components.name: Horticultural grit
components.note: Small washed stones. Makes mixes heavy and fast-draining for succulents and herbs.

components.name: Coarse sand
components.note: Sharp, washed sand only. Fine play sand clogs pores.

components.name: Horticultural charcoal
components.note: Light chunks that add air. Doesn't purify water, but helps the mix stay open.

components.name: Worm castings
components.note: A mild, slow natural food. 10% is plenty.

components.name: Akadama
components.note: Baked Japanese clay granules. Loved by bonsai growers; breaks down after a few years.

components.name: Vermiculite
components.note: Expanded mineral flakes. Good for seeds and moisture lovers.

components.name: LECA clay balls
components.note: Expanded clay pebbles. Used on their own for semi-hydro growing or as a chunky additive.

components.name: Clay soil
components.note: Very fine particles. Rich but heavy; slow to drain and can set hard when dry.

components.name: Silt
components.note: Fine, smooth particles. Fertile but packs down easily.

components.name: Loam
components.note: A mix of sand, silt and clay. The gardener's ideal soil.

components.name: Chalk
components.note: Alkaline, stony and free-draining. Can lock up iron.

components.name: Garden compost
components.note: Rotted plant waste. Feeds soil life and holds moisture.

components.name: Leaf mould
components.note: Rotted leaves. Light, spongy and slightly acid.

components.name: Lava rock
components.note: Porous volcanic rock. Heavy, airy and long-lasting.

components.name: Zeolite
components.note: A porous mineral that grabs nutrients and releases them slowly.

components.name: Rice hulls
components.note: Light husks, a renewable swap for perlite. Break down slowly.

components.name: Biochar
components.note: Charred wood that holds water and microbes. Use charged with compost.

components.name: Kanuma
components.note: Soft, acid Japanese volcanic soil for azaleas.

components.name: Calcined diatomite
components.note: Baked clay granules. Porous and stable, show dryness by colour.

components.name: Fine pine bark
components.note: Small bark chips for finer mixes.

components.name: Garden lime
components.note: Ground limestone. Use small amounts to sweeten acid soil.

components.name: Crushed oyster shell
components.note: Slowly adds calcium and raises pH.

components.name: Sterilised topsoil
components.note: Screened, heat-treated soil. Adds weight to outdoor pot mixes.

fertilizers.name: Balanced liquid feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4 weeks, spring to early autumn
fertilizers.dilution: Half to full label strength, on moist soil
fertilizers.rest: Pause from mid-autumn to early spring
fertilizers.note: An all-rounder for leafy growth.

fertilizers.name: Gentle liquid feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4–6 weeks in the growing season
fertilizers.note: For slow growers and plants that burn easily.

fertilizers.name: Cactus & succulent feed
fertilizers.rest: No food at all from October to March
fertilizers.note: Too much nitrogen makes them soft and floppy.

fertilizers.name: Orchid feed
fertilizers.dilution: Quarter strength, and flush with plain water monthly
fertilizers.rest: Reduce in winter, pause while resting
fertilizers.note: Weak and often: their roots are sensitive to salts.

fertilizers.name: Ericaceous feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4 weeks from spring to late summer
fertilizers.rest: Stop in late summer so wood can ripen
fertilizers.note: Keeps leaves green on lime-hating plants.

fertilizers.name: Citrus feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 2–3 weeks in summer, monthly in winter
fertilizers.rest: Lighter but not zero in winter
fertilizers.note: Includes iron, magnesium and zinc that citrus crave.

fertilizers.name: Flower & fruit feed
fertilizers.rest: Pause once flowering and fruiting stop
fertilizers.note: Potassium supports flowers and fruit.

fertilizers.name: Foliar feed
fertilizers.cadence: Monthly, misted or added to soaking water
fertilizers.note: For air plants and bromeliads that drink through leaves.

fertilizers.name: No fertilizer
fertilizers.cadence: Never: they catch their own food
fertilizers.note: Fertilizer burns carnivorous plant roots.

fertilizers.name: Liquid seaweed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 2 weeks in spring and summer
fertilizers.note: A gentle tonic rich in trace elements. Not a full meal.

fertilizers.name: Fish emulsion
fertilizers.note: Fast nitrogen for leafy plants. Smells for a day; best outdoors.

fertilizers.name: Worm casting tea
fertilizers.dilution: Steep a handful in 2 litres for a day
fertilizers.note: Mild and safe for seedlings and sensitive plants.

fertilizers.name: Slow-release granules
fertilizers.cadence: Once in spring, again in midsummer
fertilizers.dilution: Mix into the top of the soil at label rate
fertilizers.note: Feeds a little each time you water.

fertilizers.name: Tomato feed
fertilizers.cadence: Weekly once the first fruits set
fertilizers.rest: Stop at the end of the season
fertilizers.note: Also good for peppers, chillies and flowering plants.

fertilizers.name: Diluted succulent feed
fertilizers.note: Gentle feed for lithops and rare cacti.

fertilizers.name: Calcium and magnesium supplement
fertilizers.cadence: Every other feed in coir or LECA
fertilizers.note: Coir and LECA lack these; tomatoes and peppers need them.

fertilizers.name: Hydroponic nutrient
fertilizers.cadence: Every watering in LECA or water culture
fertilizers.note: Use only made-for-hydro feeds in semi-hydro.

fertilizers.name: No food for carnivores
fertilizers.note: Carnivorous plants catch their own food. Fertiliser kills them.

fertilizers.name: Foliar spray feed
fertilizers.note: For epiphytes like tillandsias that drink through leaves.

fertilizers.name: Bone meal
fertilizers.dilution: A small handful per large pot
fertilizers.note: For bulbs and roots. Keep away from dogs.

fertilizers.name: Blood, fish and bone
fertilizers.note: Organic, slow and steady for beds and big pots.

fertilizers.name: Pelleted chicken manure
fertilizers.note: Strong: keep away from stems and seedlings.

fertilizers.name: Compost top-dress
fertilizers.dilution: 2 cm layer on top of the soil
fertilizers.note: Feeds soil life slowly. Not a strong feed.

fertilizers.name: High-nitrogen feed
fertilizers.note: For leafy greens and grasses. Too much stops flowering.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.signs: Fine webbing, dusty speckled leaves, tiny moving dots underneath.
pests.fix: Shower the plant well, wipe leaves, raise humidity, and repeat every 5 days for three weeks. Insecticidal soap for stubborn cases.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.signs: White cottony tufts in leaf joints and under leaves, sticky residue.
pests.fix: Dab each tuft with a cotton bud dipped in rubbing alcohol, then check weekly. Isolate until clear.

pests.name: Root mealybugs
pests.signs: White waxy patches on roots and inside the pot, plant stalls.
pests.fix: Unpot, wash the roots clean, discard old soil and repot into a fresh mix and clean pot.

pests.name: Scale insects
pests.signs: Small brown or tan bumps on stems and leaf veins, sticky leaves.
pests.fix: Scrape off gently with a fingernail or soft brush, wipe with soapy water, recheck every week.

pests.name: Fungus gnats
pests.signs: Tiny black flies hovering around the soil.
pests.fix: Let the top of the soil dry out, use yellow sticky traps, and water from below for a few weeks.

pests.name: Thrips
pests.signs: Silvery streaks, black specks and twisted new leaves.
pests.fix: Shower the plant, use blue sticky traps and wipe leaves with insecticidal soap weekly.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Clusters of small green, black or pink insects on tips and buds.
pests.fix: Squash or rinse them off with water. Ladybirds and lacewings help outdoors.

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.signs: Clouds of tiny white flies rising when you brush the leaves.
pests.fix: Yellow sticky traps, and rinse leaf undersides every few days.
pests.likes: Warm, still air, tomatoes and herbs

pests.name: Cyclamen mites
pests.signs: Tightly crinkled, stunted centre leaves.
pests.fix: Hard to clear: remove damaged growth and isolate. Discard badly hit plants.

pests.name: Vine weevil
pests.signs: Notched leaf edges above, plant collapsing as grubs eat roots below.
pests.fix: Check the root ball for C-shaped grubs. Nematodes watered in late summer work well.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Ragged holes and shiny trails.
pests.fix: Night-time hand picking, copper tape on pots, and wildlife-friendly traps.

pests.name: Bulb flies
pests.signs: Grassy, flowerless leaves from soft bulbs.
pests.fix: Firm, healthy bulbs only; plant deep and mulch.

pests.name: Broad mites
pests.signs: Twisted, bronzed, stunted new growth; flowers that fail to open. The mites are too small to see.
pests.fix: Cut off the worst tips, then spray with sulphur or a miticide every 5 days for 3 weeks. Isolate the plant.
pests.likes: Warm, humid greenhouses; begonias, peppers and gerberas

pests.name: Russet mites
pests.signs: Bronze or rusty leaves and fruit, curling lower leaves, especially on tomatoes.
pests.fix: Remove affected leaves and treat with sulphur. Check neighbouring plants.

pests.name: Leaf miners
pests.signs: Pale winding trails inside the leaf.
pests.fix: Pick off mined leaves and squash the larvae at the end of each trail. Cover crops with fine mesh.

pests.name: Caterpillars
pests.signs: Large ragged holes, dark droppings, rolled leaves.
pests.fix: Pick off by hand in the evening. Fine mesh netting keeps butterflies away from brassicas.

pests.name: Snails
pests.signs: Irregular holes and silvery slime trails, often overnight.
pests.fix: Hand-pick at dusk, use copper tape on pots, and lift pots onto feet.

pests.name: Earwigs
pests.signs: Ragged holes in petals and soft leaves at night.
pests.fix: Trap them in upturned pots stuffed with straw; empty each morning.

pests.name: Springtails
pests.signs: Tiny white or grey bugs jumping on wet soil.
pests.fix: Harmless to plants: they eat fungi. Let the soil dry more and they vanish.

pests.name: Soil mites
pests.signs: Tiny brown or white specks crawling in the potting mix.
pests.fix: Mostly harmless decomposers. Repot in fresh mix if numbers are huge.

pests.name: Leafhoppers
pests.signs: Pale stippling on leaves, little insects that jump sideways.
pests.fix: Shower plants and use sticky traps. Soap spray on nymphs.

pests.name: Sawfly larvae
pests.signs: Leaves stripped to the midrib in days, often on roses and gooseberries.
pests.fix: Pick larvae off by hand and check undersides of leaves weekly.

pests.name: Lily beetle
pests.signs: Bright red beetles and messy larvae eating lily leaves.
pests.fix: Pick off beetles daily in spring; they drop when disturbed so hold a hand underneath.

pests.name: Ants
pests.signs: Ants marching up stems, often farming aphids or nesting in pots.
pests.fix: Treat the aphids or scale they protect. Stand pots in a moat of water if they nest.

pests.name: Root-knot nematodes
pests.signs: Stunted, wilting plants with knobbly swollen roots.
pests.fix: Bin the soil, repot healthy cuttings into fresh mix, and don't reuse old soil.

pests.name: Mice and squirrels
pests.signs: Dug-up bulbs, chewed seedlings, bitten fruit.
pests.fix: Cover pots with chicken wire after planting bulbs; protect fruit with mesh.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Pecked seedlings, stripped berries.
pests.fix: Net crops and berries; a few CDs or tape help briefly.

pests.name: Two-spotted mites
pests.signs: Yellow speckles, fine silk, tiny pale mites with two dark spots.
pests.fix: Rinse the plant weekly. Wipe leaf undersides. Use insecticidal soap or predatory mites for heavy cases.

pests.name: False spider mites
pests.signs: Bronze or silver patches, no webbing, tiny red flat mites.
pests.fix: Shower leaves well. Wipe undersides. Repeat weekly for a month.

pests.name: Woolly aphids
pests.signs: White waxy fluff on stems and bark, sticky leaves.
pests.fix: Brush off the fluff with a stiff brush. Spray with soap solution. Repeat weekly.

pests.name: Black aphids
pests.signs: Dense black clusters on soft tips.
pests.fix: Squash or rinse them off. Spray with soap solution weekly.

pests.name: Root aphids
pests.signs: Weak plant, white waxy powder on roots.
pests.fix: Unpot and rinse roots. Repot in fresh mix. Bin the old soil.

pests.name: Soft scale
pests.signs: Smooth brown or green bumps on stems and veins, sticky leaves.
pests.fix: Scrape them off with a fingernail. Dab with alcohol on a cotton bud. Repeat every week for a month.

pests.name: Armoured scale
pests.signs: Hard, flat grey or brown shields stuck to leaves, no honeydew.
pests.fix: Scrape off with a soft brush. Wipe with neem or horticultural oil. Repeat weekly.

pests.name: Cottony cushion scale
pests.signs: Brown scale with a white ridged egg sac.
pests.fix: Pick or scrape them off. Wipe with alcohol. Repeat weekly.

pests.name: Long-tailed mealybugs
pests.signs: White fluffy bugs with long tail threads.
pests.fix: Dab each one with alcohol. Spray with soap solution weekly. Check leaf joints.

pests.name: Greenhouse whitefly
pests.signs: Tiny white flies that rise in a cloud when touched.
pests.fix: Hang yellow sticky traps. Spray leaf undersides with soap weekly. Vacuum adults gently.

pests.name: Western flower thrips
pests.signs: Silver scars, black dots, streaked petals.
pests.fix: Use blue sticky traps. Remove old flowers. Spray with soap weekly for a month.

pests.name: Chilli thrips
pests.signs: Curled, bronzed new leaves and buds.
pests.fix: Cut off badly damaged tips. Spray soap or neem weekly. Repeat for a month.

pests.name: Shore flies
pests.signs: Dark flies with pale wing spots near wet soil and algae.
pests.fix: Let the soil surface dry. Scrape off algae. Use yellow sticky traps.

pests.name: Fruit flies
pests.signs: Small tan flies with red eyes near fruit or compost.
pests.fix: Remove rotting fruit. Set a cup of cider vinegar with a drop of soap.

pests.name: Cutworms
pests.signs: Seedlings cut off at the soil line overnight.
pests.fix: Search the soil at night and remove grubs. Use a collar of card around young stems.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Green caterpillars and holes in cabbage leaves.
pests.fix: Pick them off. Cover crops with fine mesh. Squash yellow egg clusters under leaves.

pests.name: Tomato hornworm
pests.signs: Large green caterpillars, stripped tomato leaves, dark droppings.
pests.fix: Pick them off by hand. Check under leaves at dusk.

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.signs: Tiny jumping beetles and shot holes in leaves.
pests.fix: Cover young crops with mesh. Keep seedlings well watered.

pests.name: Japanese beetles
pests.signs: Metallic green beetles, lacy skeleton leaves.
pests.fix: Knock them into soapy water in the morning. Avoid scented traps nearby.

pests.name: Rose sawfly
pests.signs: Rose leaves rolled tight or eaten to lace.
pests.fix: Pick off rolled leaves. Squash larvae. Rinse with a hose.

pests.name: Box tree caterpillar
pests.signs: Webbing and stripped box leaves.
pests.fix: Pick caterpillars off. Prune webbed parts. Use pheromone traps to monitor.

pests.name: Woodlice
pests.signs: Grey armoured bugs under pots, rarely harmful.
pests.fix: Clear debris and lift pots onto feet. Let the soil surface dry.

pests.name: Millipedes
pests.signs: Thin dark worm-like bugs curling in the soil.
pests.fix: Mostly harmless. Let soil dry and remove rotting matter.

pests.name: Gnat larvae
pests.signs: Clear thread-like larvae with black heads in wet soil.
pests.fix: Let the top of the soil dry. Water with BTI. Use yellow traps for adults.

pests.name: Leaf beetles
pests.signs: Small beetles and their larvae chewing holes.
pests.fix: Pick them off. Check under leaves. Clear fallen leaves in autumn.

pests.name: Rosemary beetle
pests.signs: Shiny purple-green beetles on rosemary and lavender.
pests.fix: Shake them onto paper and remove. Check weekly.

pests.name: Psyllids
pests.signs: Tiny jumping bugs, curled sticky leaves, white wax.
pests.fix: Spray with soap solution weekly. Prune heavily infested tips.

pests.name: Bay sucker
pests.signs: Thick, yellow, curled edges on bay leaves.
pests.fix: Pick off curled leaves. Spray soap on new growth.

pests.name: Gall mites
pests.signs: Raised bumps, felty patches or swollen buds.
pests.fix: Prune and bin affected parts. Plants usually cope fine.

pests.name: Lace bugs
pests.signs: Pale speckled upper leaves, black spots below.
pests.fix: Spray leaf undersides with soap solution. Repeat weekly.

pests.name: Orchid root mealybugs
pests.signs: White cotton in orchid roots and bark.
pests.fix: Unpot and rinse roots. Dab with alcohol. Repot in fresh bark.

pests.name: Stored plant pests
pests.signs: Tiny brown beetles in dried herbs, seeds or bulbs.
pests.fix: Freeze stored seeds for 3 days. Keep them in sealed jars.

pests.name: Squirrels
pests.signs: Bulbs dug up, pots scattered, bitten fruit.
pests.fix: Cover pots with wire mesh. Plant bulbs deeper. Don't leave food out.

pests.name: Cats
pests.signs: Chewed leaves, dug soil, litter use in pots.
pests.fix: Cover soil with stones or mesh. Offer cat grass. Move toxic plants out of reach.

symptoms.name: Yellow lower leaves
symptoms.looks: Older leaves near the base turn yellow, one or two at a time.
fixes: One old leaf now and then is normal: snip it.
If several go at once and soil is wet, water less.
If soil is fine, feed in spring and summer.

symptoms.name: Yellow new leaves
symptoms.looks: Fresh growth comes in pale or yellow, often with green veins.
fixes: Use a feed with micronutrients.
Rainwater for acid lovers.
Move away from cold floors and windows.

symptoms.name: Yellowing all over
symptoms.looks: Leaves fade and yellow across the whole plant.
fixes: Check the roots and let the soil dry.
Brighter spot.
Fresh soil and a pot one size up in spring.

symptoms.name: Brown, crispy tips
symptoms.looks: Leaf tips and edges dry out and go papery brown.
causes: Salt or fluoride from tap water and fertilizer
fixes: Raise humidity by grouping plants.
Water deeply, then on time.
Flush the soil and use rain or filtered water.

symptoms.name: Soft brown patches
symptoms.looks: Dark, mushy areas, sometimes with a yellow ring.
fixes: Cut affected leaves with clean scissors.
Water less and improve airflow.
Keep leaves dry when watering.

symptoms.name: Bleached or scorched patches
symptoms.looks: Pale, crispy or brown patches on the sunniest side.
causes: Sunburn after a sudden move into strong light
fixes: Move back from the window or filter with a sheer curtain.
Damaged spots won't heal, but new leaves will be fine.

symptoms.name: Droopy with dry soil
symptoms.looks: Leaves hang limp and the pot feels light.
fixes: Water deeply until it drains, or bottom-soak for 30 minutes.
It should perk up within a day.

symptoms.name: Droopy with wet soil
symptoms.looks: Limp leaves although the soil is soggy.
causes: Root rot: roots can't drink when drowned
fixes: Unpot, trim black mushy roots, repot in fresh airy mix.
Water only when the top dries.

symptoms.name: Leggy, stretched growth
symptoms.looks: Long gaps between leaves, stems leaning to the window.
fixes: Brighter spot or a grow light.
Prune leggy stems and root the cuttings.

symptoms.name: Small new leaves
symptoms.looks: Each new leaf is smaller than the last.
fixes: More light first.
Feed in the growing season.
Check whether roots fill the pot.

symptoms.name: Sudden leaf drop
symptoms.looks: Healthy-looking leaves fall without warning.
causes: A move, draught or temperature shock
Very dry or very wet roots
fixes: Choose a steady spot and leave it there.
Check soil moisture and adjust.

symptoms.name: Curling leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves roll inward or cup downward.
fixes: Feel the soil and water if dry.
Move away from heaters.
Look under the leaves.

symptoms.name: Pale rings or blotches
symptoms.looks: Pale rings or spots, often on velvety leaves.
fixes: Water the soil, not the leaves, with room-temperature water.

symptoms.name: White powder on leaves
symptoms.looks: A dusty white coating that wipes off.
fixes: Remove worst leaves, improve airflow, water the soil not the leaves.

symptoms.name: Sticky leaves
symptoms.looks: A shiny, sticky film, sometimes with black mould.
fixes: Look for the insects under leaves and on stems and wipe them off.

symptoms.name: Fine webbing
symptoms.looks: Thin webs between leaves and stems, speckled leaves.
fixes: Shower the plant and raise humidity; repeat weekly.

symptoms.name: White fluffy bits
symptoms.looks: Cotton-like tufts in leaf joints.
fixes: Dab with alcohol on a cotton bud and repeat weekly.

symptoms.name: Tiny flies around the soil
symptoms.looks: Small black flies rising when you water.
causes: Fungus gnats from constantly damp compost
fixes: Let the top dry, use sticky traps, water from below.

symptoms.name: Mould on the soil
symptoms.looks: White fuzz on the surface of the compost.
causes: Damp, still air and soggy topsoil

Shower and isolate.
Remove spotted leaves.

Repot into a heavier, bigger pot.

Repot or feed in the growing season.

Repot into fresh, airy mix.

symptoms.name: Fruit or flowers dropping early

Steady watering and temperature.

Cut back to a variegated leaf.

Water the soil only.

Wipe and treat.

Water the soil, not the leaves.

Water only when the top inch is dry.

Water the soil, not the leaves.

Shower and wipe leaves.
Move out of harsh sun.

symptoms.name: Purple or reddish leaves

Feed with a balanced feed.

symptoms.name: Very dark, floppy leaves

Feed less often.

symptoms.name: Leaves curling up

symptoms.name: Cupped leaves

Water evenly.

Water evenly.

symptoms.name: New leaf stuck unfurling

symptoms.name: Leaning toward the window

symptoms.name: Green leaves falling

symptoms.name: Soft, limp leaves

Treat the pest and repeat weekly.

Water marks wipe off with a damp cloth.

symptoms.name: No growth at all

Water before soil gets bone dry.

fixes: Stop watering and let it dry fully.
Remove mushy leaves.
Use a gritty mix and a pot with holes.

symptoms.name: Wrinkled, thin succulent leaves
symptoms.looks: Plump leaves go flat and wrinkled.
fixes: Water deeply until it drains.
If it doesn't plump up in days, check the roots.

symptoms.name: Stretching succulent
symptoms.looks: Rosette opens up and the stem grows tall.
fixes: Move to the sunniest window.
Behead and re-root the top in spring.

symptoms.name: Leaves falling off at a touch
symptoms.looks: Leaves drop when you brush them.
fixes: Let the soil dry fully.
Root the fallen leaves.

symptoms.name: Succulent turning red or orange
symptoms.looks: Leaves blush red, pink or orange.
fixes: This is usually healthy stress colour.
Only worry if leaves shrivel or scorch.

symptoms.name: Cactus turning yellow
symptoms.looks: A green cactus turns yellow or pale.
fixes: Adapt it to sun slowly.
Water less, especially in winter.
Check the base for soft spots.

symptoms.name: Brown base on cactus
symptoms.looks: The base turns brown and hard.
fixes: Hard, dry brown is normal ageing.
Soft or wet brown is rot: cut above it.

symptoms.name: Soft spot on cactus
symptoms.looks: A squishy, dark patch on the cactus.
fixes: Cut out the soft part to clean tissue.
Dust with sulphur or let it dry for days.
Water only when dry.

symptoms.name: Cactus getting thin at the top
symptoms.looks: The tip grows narrower and pale.
fixes: Move to more sun, slowly.
The thin part won't widen; new growth will be normal.

symptoms.name: Wrinkly, limp orchid leaves
symptoms.looks: Moth orchid leaves go soft and wrinkled.
fixes: Check roots: green or silver and firm is good.
Soak the pot for 15 minutes when roots are silver.
Repot into fresh bark if roots are mushy.

symptoms.name: Orchid bottom leaf yellow
symptoms.looks: The lowest orchid leaf turns yellow.
fixes: One old leaf now and then is normal.
Check roots if more yellow fast.

symptoms.name: Orchid won't rebloom
symptoms.looks: Leaves grow, but no new flower spike.
fixes: Give 2 to 4 weeks of nights near 15 °C in autumn.
Move to a bright east window.
Feed lightly every other watering.

symptoms.name: Mushy orchid roots
symptoms.looks: Roots are brown, hollow or mushy.
fixes: Repot into fresh bark.
Trim dead roots with clean scissors.
Water only when roots turn silver.

symptoms.name: Orchid spike turning yellow
symptoms.looks: The flower stem goes yellow then brown.
fixes: Cut it back to the base once brown.
A still-green spike may rebloom from a node.

symptoms.name: Baby plant on orchid spike
symptoms.looks: A small plant grows on the flower stem.
fixes: Leave it until it has roots 5 cm long.
Then cut and pot it in fine bark.

symptoms.name: Crispy fern fronds
symptoms.looks: Fronds brown and crisp from the tips.
fixes: Keep the soil lightly moist.
Raise humidity; bathrooms suit ferns.
Cut crisp fronds at the base.

symptoms.name: Fern shedding tiny leaflets
symptoms.looks: Little leaflets rain down on the floor.
fixes: Never let the soil dry out fully.
Raise humidity.
Trim bare fronds.

symptoms.name: Brown dots under fern fronds
symptoms.looks: Neat rows of brown dots on the underside.
fixes: These are spores, not pests.
Scale is irregular and scrapes off; spores sit in tidy rows.

symptoms.name: Calathea leaves curling
symptoms.looks: Leaves roll up during the day.
fixes: Water when the top 2 cm is dry.
Raise humidity.
Move away from direct sun.

symptoms.name: Calathea crispy edges
symptoms.looks: Brown crispy edges and tips.
fixes: Use rain or filtered water.
Raise humidity.
Trim edges along the leaf shape.

symptoms.name: Leaves rising at night
symptoms.looks: Leaves fold up in the evening.
fixes: This is normal and healthy.
Only worry if they stay folded all day.

symptoms.name: Fiddle leaf fig brown spots
symptoms.looks: Dark brown spots, often from the middle or edge.
fixes: Let the top 5 cm dry before watering.
Check roots for rot.
Remove the worst leaves.

symptoms.name: Tiny red dots on new fig leaves
symptoms.looks: Small red-brown dots on young leaves.
fixes: Water evenly and less at once.
Dots usually fade as leaves mature.

symptoms.name: Fiddle leaf fig dropping leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves fall after a move or season change.
fixes: Find a bright spot and leave it there.
Keep away from doors and vents.
Water only when the top dries.

symptoms.name: Monstera leaves without holes
symptoms.looks: New leaves come out whole.
fixes: Give bright, indirect light.
Add a moss pole.
Young plants make solid leaves; it's normal.

symptoms.name: Monstera yellow leaves
symptoms.looks: Lower or several leaves turn yellow.
fixes: Water when the top half is dry.
Repot if roots circle.
Feed in spring and summer.

symptoms.name: Water drops on leaf tips
symptoms.looks: Drops of water appear at leaf edges in the morning.
fixes: Harmless, but a sign the soil is very wet.
Water a little less.

symptoms.name: Pothos yellow leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves yellow along the vines.
fixes: Let the top half dry.
Move to brighter light.
Trim yellow leaves.

symptoms.name: Pothos with tiny new leaves
symptoms.looks: Vines grow long with small leaves.
fixes: Move it closer to light.
Let it climb; climbing makes bigger leaves.
Feed in the growing season.

symptoms.name: Snake plant mushy leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves go soft at the base and fall over.
fixes: Stop watering and unpot to check.
Cut away mushy parts and root healthy leaf pieces.
Water once a month or less in winter.

symptoms.name: Snake plant wrinkled leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves look thin, curled and wrinkled.
fixes: Water deeply if bone dry.
Check roots if the soil is wet.

symptoms.name: Snake plant leaves flopping
symptoms.looks: Tall leaves bend and fall outward.
fixes: Give brighter light.
Water less.
Tie floppy leaves loosely while new ones firm up.

symptoms.name: ZZ plant yellowing
symptoms.looks: Stems and leaves turn yellow.
fixes: Let the soil dry fully between waterings.
Check the rhizomes are firm.

symptoms.name: Peace lily collapsing
symptoms.looks: The whole plant flops dramatically.
fixes: Water thoroughly; it perks up in hours.
Water a little earlier next time.

symptoms.name: Peace lily brown tips
symptoms.looks: Leaf tips brown and dry.
fixes: Use filtered or rainwater.
Flush the soil.
Trim the tips.

symptoms.name: Peace lily flowers turn green
symptoms.looks: White flowers fade to green.
fixes: Normal: cut old flowers at the base.

symptoms.name: Dracaena brown tips
symptoms.looks: Brown tips with a yellow edge.
fixes: Use filtered or rainwater.
Avoid perlite with lots of fluoride.
Trim tips at an angle.

symptoms.name: Rubber plant dropping lower leaves
symptoms.looks: Bottom leaves yellow and fall.
fixes: Give bright light.
Water when the top half dries.
Keep above 15 °C.

symptoms.name: Spider plant brown tips
symptoms.looks: Leaf tips brown and dry.
fixes: Use filtered or rainwater.
Flush the pot.
Trim tips.

symptoms.name: Spider plant with no babies
symptoms.looks: No runners or plantlets form.
fixes: Give bright light.
A snug pot encourages runners.
Mature plants make babies in spring.

symptoms.name: Aloe leaves lying flat
symptoms.looks: Leaves splay out and flop.
fixes: Move to a sunny window.
Water less often.

symptoms.name: Aloe turning brown or red
symptoms.looks: Leaves turn brown, red or orange.
fixes: Some colour in sun is normal.
Soft brown means too much water.

symptoms.name: Jade dropping leaves
symptoms.looks: Plump leaves fall off.
fixes: Water only when fully dry.
Keep it warm and bright.

symptoms.name: String of pearls shrivelling
symptoms.looks: Pearls go flat or dry at the crown.
fixes: Water when pearls start to wrinkle.
Keep the crown dry and the pot shallow.
Re-root healthy strands on top of the soil.

symptoms.name: Herbs going woody
symptoms.looks: Stems turn tough with few leaves.
fixes: Pinch tips often to keep plants bushy.
Replace old basil and coriander each season.

symptoms.name: Herbs bolting to flower
symptoms.looks: Herbs shoot up and flower, leaves turn bitter.
fixes: Pinch flower buds early.
Sow coriander and lettuce in cooler months.
Sow small batches often.

symptoms.name: Basil leaves turning black
symptoms.looks: Black patches on basil leaves.
fixes: Keep basil warm.
Water the soil in the morning.
Remove spotted leaves.

symptoms.name: Orange spots on mint
symptoms.looks: Orange pustules under mint leaves.
fixes: Cut the plant hard and bin the leaves.
Water at the base and give airflow.

symptoms.name: Tomato lower leaves yellow
symptoms.looks: Bottom tomato leaves yellow and spot.
fixes: Remove lower leaves touching soil.
Feed with a tomato feed.
Mulch to stop soil splash.

symptoms.name: Tomato leaves curling
symptoms.looks: Leaves roll up tightly.
fixes: Usually harmless; keep watering steady.
Give afternoon shade in heatwaves.

symptoms.name: Pepper flowers dropping
symptoms.looks: Flowers fall without fruit.
fixes: Water steadily.
Shake the plant gently to pollinate.
Wait for milder weather.

symptoms.name: Bitter lettuce
symptoms.looks: Leaves taste bitter and stems stretch.
fixes: Grow lettuce in cool seasons.
Pick young leaves often.

symptoms.name: Strawberries not fruiting
symptoms.looks: Lots of leaves and runners, no berries.
fixes: Give full sun.
Cut runners off.
Feed with potassium-rich feed.

symptoms.name: Citrus leaves yellowing
symptoms.looks: Lemon or orange leaves turn yellow.
fixes: Use a citrus feed in the growing season.
Let the soil dry a little between waterings.
Give the sunniest spot.

symptoms.name: Citrus dropping leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves fall, often in winter.
fixes: Give the brightest, coolest spot inside.
Raise humidity.
Water less in winter.

symptoms.name: Bulbs not flowering
symptoms.looks: Bulbs make leaves but no flowers.
causes: Leaves cut too early last year
fixes: Let leaves die back naturally after blooming.
Give bulbs a cold period.
Divide crowded clumps.

symptoms.name: Christmas cactus dropping buds
symptoms.looks: Buds form, then fall off.
fixes: Don't move it once buds form.
Keep it cool and away from heaters.
Water evenly.

symptoms.name: Poinsettia dropping leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves fall soon after buying.
fixes: Keep it warm and bright.
Water only when the top dries.
Never leave it in a wet wrapper.

symptoms.name: Bonsai yellowing
symptoms.looks: Leaves on a bonsai turn yellow.
causes: Indoor bonsai of an outdoor tree
fixes: Check the soil daily; small pots dry fast.
Many bonsai trees need to live outdoors.

symptoms.name: Terrarium mouldy or foggy
symptoms.looks: Constant fog and mould inside.
fixes: Open the lid for a few days.
Remove mouldy bits.
Water much less.

symptoms.name: Plant not climbing moss pole
symptoms.looks: Aerial roots ignore the pole.
fixes: Keep the pole moist.
Tie stems so nodes touch the pole.

symptoms.name: Ivy drying out
symptoms.looks: English ivy goes crispy and dusty.
fixes: Shower it and check for mites.
Keep it cool and humid.

symptoms.name: Tradescantia going bare
symptoms.looks: Long vines with dead leaves near the soil.
fixes: Pinch tips and replant cuttings in the pot.
Give bright light.

symptoms.name: Alocasia losing leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves die one by one until it seems gone.
causes: Dormancy from cold or low light
fixes: Check for mites.
Keep the bulb-like corm slightly moist and warm.
It often regrows in spring.

symptoms.name: Hoya won't bloom
symptoms.looks: Healthy hoya, no flowers.
fixes: Give bright light.
Don't cut old flower spurs.
Keep it slightly pot-bound.

symptoms.name: Bird of paradise split leaves
symptoms.looks: Leaves tear along the veins.
fixes: It's normal for this plant.
Raise humidity to keep new leaves neater.

symptoms.name: Air plant browning
symptoms.looks: Tips brown or the centre rots.
fixes: Soak 20 minutes weekly.
Shake out and dry upside down within 4 hours.

symptoms.name: Bromeliad dying after flowering
symptoms.looks: The mother plant fades after blooming.
fixes: Normal: it makes pups first.
Pot pups when they're a third of the mother's size.

symptoms.name: Venus flytrap traps turning black
symptoms.looks: Traps blacken and die.
fixes: Use rain or distilled water only.
Don't trigger traps for fun.
Give full sun.

symptoms.name: Roots pushing up out of the soil
symptoms.looks: Roots surface and lift the plant.
fixes: Repot into a slightly bigger pot.
Or top-dress with fresh mix.

symptoms.name: White crust on pot or soil
symptoms.looks: White or yellow crust on the soil or pot rim.
fixes: Scrape off the crust.
Flush the pot with plain water.
Feed at half strength.

symptoms.name: Leaves pointing down
symptoms.looks: Leaves hang down from the stems.
causes: Natural for some plants at night
fixes: Check the soil moisture.
Adjust watering.

diseases.name: Root rot
diseases.signs: Wilting despite wet soil, yellow leaves, a sour smell, black mushy roots.
diseases.why: Roots starved of air in waterlogged soil.
diseases.fix: Unpot, cut away soft roots, repot into fresh airy mix in a clean pot, water sparingly.
diseases.prevent: Pots with holes, airy mixes, and water only when needed.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.signs: A white powdery film on leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus that loves dry roots and still, humid air.
diseases.fix: Remove badly hit leaves, increase airflow, keep leaves dry.
diseases.prevent: Space plants out and water the soil, not the leaves.

diseases.name: Leaf spot
diseases.signs: Brown or black spots, often with yellow halos.
diseases.why: Fungi or bacteria spread by water splashes.
diseases.fix: Snip spotted leaves, water at the base, improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Keep foliage dry and clean your tools.

diseases.name: Grey mould
diseases.signs: Fuzzy grey mould on flowers, buds or soft leaves.
diseases.why: Cool, damp, stagnant air.
diseases.fix: Remove affected parts and ventilate.
diseases.prevent: Deadhead faded flowers and avoid crowding.

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.signs: Orange or brown powdery pustules under leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus that spreads in damp weather.
diseases.fix: Remove affected leaves and bin them, not compost.
diseases.prevent: Water in the morning at soil level.

diseases.name: Black spot
diseases.signs: Black blotches with yellowing on rose leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus that spreads in wet weather.
diseases.fix: Collect fallen leaves, remove affected ones.
diseases.prevent: Water the soil, mulch, and choose resistant roses.

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.signs: Seedlings collapse at soil level.
diseases.why: Fungi in cold, wet compost.
diseases.fix: Sow in fresh compost, water from below, and give airflow.
diseases.prevent: Clean pots and don't overwater seedlings.

diseases.name: Sooty mould
diseases.signs: A black film that wipes off the leaves.
diseases.why: Fungus feeding on the honeydew of sap-sucking pests.
diseases.fix: Deal with the pests, then wipe leaves clean.
diseases.prevent: Regular pest checks.

diseases.name: Crown rot
diseases.signs: The centre of a rosette turns soft and brown.
diseases.why: Water sitting in the crown.
diseases.fix: Remove rotted tissue, keep the crown dry.
diseases.prevent: Water around the edge of the pot.

diseases.name: Oedema (corky bumps)
diseases.signs: Small blister-like bumps under leaves that turn corky.
diseases.why: Roots take up water faster than leaves can release it.
diseases.fix: Water less and increase light and airflow.
diseases.prevent: Water in the morning, avoid cold soggy soil.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.signs: Yellow patches on top of leaves, grey-purple fuzz underneath.
diseases.why: Cool, damp weather and wet leaves.
diseases.fix: Remove infected leaves, water at the base in the morning, improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Space plants, avoid wetting leaves, choose resistant varieties (basil, impatiens).

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.signs: Sunken brown or black spots with dark rims, often along the veins.
diseases.why: A fungus spread by splashing water.
diseases.fix: Cut out infected parts, keep leaves dry, clean tools.
diseases.prevent: Water the soil, not the plant; good airflow.

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf spot
diseases.signs: Water-soaked spots with yellow halos that turn brown, sometimes smelly.
diseases.why: Bacteria entering through wet leaves or wounds.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted leaves, stop misting, isolate the plant.
diseases.prevent: Keep foliage dry and use clean scissors.

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
diseases.signs: One side of the plant wilts and yellows; brown streaks inside the stem.
diseases.why: A soil fungus that blocks water flow.
diseases.fix: There's no cure: discard the plant and its soil.
diseases.prevent: Fresh sterile mix and resistant varieties.

diseases.name: Stem rot
diseases.signs: Brown, soft stem at soil level, white threads, collapse.
diseases.why: Fungi in warm, wet soil.
diseases.fix: Take healthy cuttings and start again; discard the soil.
diseases.prevent: Don't bury stems too deep and let the surface dry.

diseases.name: Blossom end rot
diseases.signs: A sunken dark patch at the bottom of tomatoes and peppers.
diseases.why: Uneven watering stops calcium reaching the fruit.
diseases.fix: Water steadily and deeply; remove affected fruit.
diseases.prevent: Mulch pots and never let them swing from soaked to bone dry.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.signs: Brown blotches on leaves and stems, brown rotting fruit, fast spread in wet weather.
diseases.why: A water mould carried on the wind in warm, wet summers.
diseases.fix: Remove and bin infected growth at once (not compost).
diseases.prevent: Grow under cover, water at the base, choose blight-resistant tomatoes.

diseases.name: Mosaic virus
diseases.signs: Mottled light and dark patches, crinkled leaves, stunted growth.
diseases.why: Viruses spread by aphids, hands or tools.
diseases.fix: No cure: bin the plant and wash hands and tools.
diseases.prevent: Control aphids and buy healthy plants.

diseases.name: Lime-induced chlorosis
diseases.signs: Yellow leaves with green veins on acid lovers.
diseases.why: Alkaline water or soil locks up iron.
diseases.fix: Water with rain water, use ericaceous feed with chelated iron.
diseases.prevent: Ericaceous compost and rain water for acid lovers.

diseases.name: Sunscald
diseases.signs: Bleached white or papery brown patches on the sunny side.
diseases.why: A sudden move into strong sun, or water droplets in hot sun.
diseases.fix: Move back to softer light; cut damaged leaves once new ones grow.
diseases.prevent: Acclimatise plants to stronger light over 1–2 weeks.

diseases.name: Cold damage
diseases.signs: Dark, glassy or mushy leaves after a cold night or draught.
diseases.why: Tropical cells burst below about 10 °C.
diseases.fix: Cut damaged parts once it warms and keep it warm and slightly dry.
diseases.prevent: Keep tropicals away from cold glass and doors in winter.

diseases.name: Transplant shock
diseases.signs: Wilting or dropping leaves just after repotting or moving.
diseases.why: Roots were disturbed or conditions changed.
diseases.fix: Steady light, normal watering, no feed for a month.
diseases.prevent: Repot in spring and disturb roots gently.

diseases.name: Orchid crown rot
diseases.signs: Black, mushy centre where leaves meet.
diseases.why: Water left sitting in the crown.
diseases.fix: Dab with cinnamon or 3 % hydrogen peroxide, keep dry, hope for a keiki.
diseases.prevent: Water in the morning, tilt to drain the crown.

diseases.name: Rose and pelargonium rust
diseases.signs: Orange powdery pustules under leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus spread in humid, still air.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted leaves and improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Water at the base and space plants out.

diseases.name: Pythium root rot
diseases.signs: Brown, soft roots whose outer layer slips off; plants wilt.
diseases.why: A water mould in cold, soggy soil.
diseases.fix: Unpot. Cut off soft roots. Repot in fresh, airy mix. Water less.
diseases.prevent: Use pots with holes and let soil dry slightly between waterings.

diseases.name: Phytophthora rot
diseases.signs: Dark lesions at the stem base, sudden wilting.
diseases.why: A water mould spread by splashing, wet soil.
diseases.fix: Remove badly affected plants. Repot healthy ones in fresh mix. Disinfect pots.
diseases.prevent: Good drainage and clean pots.

diseases.name: Rhizoctonia stem rot
diseases.signs: Brown sunken lesions at soil level.
diseases.why: A soil fungus in warm, damp mix.
diseases.fix: Cut out infected stems. Repot in fresh mix. Keep the base dry.
diseases.prevent: Use fresh mix and avoid deep planting.

diseases.name: Stem rot
diseases.signs: Soft, dark stem sections that collapse.
diseases.why: Fungi or bacteria entering through wounds in wet conditions.
diseases.fix: Cut well above the rot. Root clean cuttings. Bin the rest.
diseases.prevent: Water less and keep stems dry.

diseases.name: Bacterial soft rot
diseases.signs: Mushy, foul-smelling tissue that spreads fast.
diseases.why: Bacteria in warm, wet wounds.
diseases.fix: Remove all soft parts at once. Let cuts dry. Isolate the plant.
diseases.prevent: Avoid wounds and wet stems.

diseases.name: Erwinia rot
diseases.signs: Slimy, smelly rot on bulbs, cuttings or stems.
diseases.why: Bacteria thriving in warm, wet conditions.
diseases.fix: Cut out all mushy tissue. Let it dry. Bin badly hit plants.
diseases.prevent: Dry cuts before potting and water lightly.

diseases.name: Xanthomonas leaf spot
diseases.signs: Yellow-edged, water-soaked spots, often on anthuriums and aroids.
diseases.why: Bacteria spread by splashing water.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted leaves. Keep leaves dry. Clean tools between plants.
diseases.prevent: Water at the soil and space plants out.

diseases.name: Pseudomonas leaf spot
diseases.signs: Dark, greasy spots with yellow halos.
diseases.why: Bacteria in cool, wet conditions.
diseases.fix: Remove affected leaves. Keep leaves dry. Improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Morning watering at the base.

diseases.name: Fire blight
diseases.signs: Shoots look scorched and bent like a shepherd's crook.
diseases.why: A bacterium of pears, apples and quince.
diseases.fix: Cut 30 cm below the damage. Disinfect pruners between cuts. Bin the clippings.
diseases.prevent: Prune in dry weather and avoid heavy nitrogen.

diseases.name: Cercospora leaf spot
diseases.signs: Small grey-centred spots with dark borders.
diseases.why: A fungus spread in warm, wet weather.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted leaves. Water at the base. Give airflow.
diseases.prevent: Keep leaves dry and clear debris.

diseases.name: Alternaria leaf spot
diseases.signs: Brown spots with target rings.
diseases.why: A fungus on stressed or wet leaves.
diseases.fix: Remove affected leaves. Mulch to stop splashing. Feed the plant well.
diseases.prevent: Water at the base and rotate crops.

diseases.name: Septoria leaf spot
diseases.signs: Many small grey spots with dark edges on tomato leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus spread by rain splash.
diseases.fix: Remove lower spotted leaves. Mulch the soil. Water at the base.
diseases.prevent: Rotate crops and space plants.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.signs: Brown target spots on lower tomato and potato leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus that lives in soil and old debris.
diseases.fix: Remove infected leaves. Mulch. Water at the base.
diseases.prevent: Clear old plants and rotate beds.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.signs: Large brown greasy patches, white fuzz below, fruit rots.
diseases.why: A water mould in warm, wet weather.
diseases.fix: Remove and bin infected plants. Don't compost them.
diseases.prevent: Grow resistant varieties and keep leaves dry.

diseases.name: Verticillium wilt
diseases.signs: Leaves wilt on one side, brown streaks inside stems.
diseases.why: A soil fungus that blocks water flow.
diseases.fix: Remove badly affected plants. Don't replant the same family there. Bin the soil.
diseases.prevent: Use fresh mix and resistant varieties.

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.signs: Sudden wilting of healthy-looking plants.
diseases.why: Bacteria in the stems, often spread by beetles.
diseases.fix: Remove infected plants. Control beetles. Clean tools.
diseases.prevent: Rotate crops and use clean soil.

diseases.name: Clubroot
diseases.signs: Swollen, distorted roots on cabbage family plants.
diseases.why: A soil organism favoured by acid, wet soil.
diseases.fix: Remove plants with roots. Raise soil pH with garden lime. Don't grow brassicas there for years.
diseases.prevent: Raise brassicas in clean pots and lime acid soil.

diseases.name: White mould
diseases.signs: White cottony growth with black seed-like bodies on stems.
diseases.why: Sclerotinia fungus in cool, damp weather.
diseases.fix: Remove infected plants. Don't compost them. Improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Space plants and water in the morning.

diseases.name: Grey mould on stems
diseases.signs: Grey fuzzy rot on stems and cuttings.
diseases.why: Botrytis in cool, still, damp air.
diseases.fix: Cut out infected parts. Improve airflow. Water less.
diseases.prevent: Keep cuttings ventilated and remove dead leaves.

diseases.name: Canker
diseases.signs: Sunken, cracked dead patches on stems or bark.
diseases.why: Fungi or bacteria entering wounds.
diseases.fix: Cut out branches below the canker. Disinfect pruners. Bin the wood.
diseases.prevent: Prune cleanly in dry weather.

diseases.name: Dieback
diseases.signs: Shoots die from the tips backward.
diseases.why: Root damage, cold or infection.
diseases.fix: Prune back to healthy wood. Check roots and drainage.
diseases.prevent: Steady care and clean pruning.

diseases.name: Peach leaf curl
diseases.signs: Red, puckered, blistered leaves in spring.
diseases.why: A fungus spread by spring rain.
diseases.fix: Remove affected leaves. Feed and water well. Shelter the tree from rain in late winter.
diseases.prevent: Cover the tree in late winter.

diseases.name: Scab
diseases.signs: Dark scabby spots on leaves and fruit.
diseases.why: A fungus in wet springs.
diseases.fix: Remove fallen leaves. Prune for airflow. Pick off spotted fruit.
diseases.prevent: Grow resistant varieties and clear debris.

diseases.name: Brown rot
diseases.signs: Fruit turns brown with rings of pale pustules.
diseases.why: A fungus entering through damaged fruit.
diseases.fix: Pick off all rotten fruit, including on the ground. Prune out dead shoots.
diseases.prevent: Thin fruit and remove mummified fruit.

diseases.name: Anthurium blight
diseases.signs: Yellow-edged wedges spreading in from the leaf edge.
diseases.why: Bacteria spread by water and tools.
diseases.fix: Remove affected leaves. Keep leaves dry. Disinfect scissors.
diseases.prevent: Water the soil only and isolate new plants.

diseases.name: Ficus leaf blight
diseases.signs: Large brown patches on fig leaves, often at the edges.
diseases.why: Fungus on stressed, wet leaves.
diseases.fix: Remove damaged leaves. Keep leaves dry. Water evenly.
diseases.prevent: Stable care and good airflow.

diseases.name: Orchid black rot
diseases.signs: Black, spreading patches on leaves or pseudobulbs.
diseases.why: Water moulds in cool, wet conditions.
diseases.fix: Cut out black tissue with a clean blade. Dust with cinnamon. Keep it dry.
diseases.prevent: Water in the morning and keep water off leaves.

diseases.name: Orchid petal blight
diseases.signs: Small pink or brown spots on orchid flowers.
diseases.why: Botrytis in cool, humid air.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted flowers. Increase airflow. Keep flowers dry.
diseases.prevent: Avoid misting flowers.

diseases.name: Succulent rot
diseases.signs: Black or translucent mushy stems and leaves.
diseases.why: Wet soil plus cold or poor drainage.
diseases.fix: Cut above the rot. Let cuttings callus for days. Replant in gritty mix.
diseases.prevent: Gritty mix and soak-and-dry watering.

diseases.name: Corky scab
diseases.signs: Rough tan patches on cactus skin.
diseases.why: Stress from humidity, cold or poor light.
diseases.fix: Improve light and airflow. Scabs won't vanish but new growth will be clean.
diseases.prevent: Bright light and dry winters.

diseases.name: Cactus stem rot
diseases.signs: Soft brown or black spots that spread.
diseases.why: Fungi entering through wet soil or wounds.
diseases.fix: Cut out all soft tissue. Let it dry fully. Repot in dry gritty mix.
diseases.prevent: Water only in warm months, and lightly.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew on succulents
diseases.signs: White dusty spots on leaves, sometimes scarred.
diseases.why: A fungus in still, humid air.
diseases.fix: Wipe off spots. Improve airflow. Spray with diluted milk weekly.
diseases.prevent: Space plants and give good light.

diseases.name: Impatiens downy mildew
diseases.signs: Yellowing leaves with white fuzz below, plants collapse.
diseases.why: A water mould in cool, wet weather.
diseases.fix: Remove and bin infected plants. Don't replant impatiens in that soil.
diseases.prevent: Choose resistant bedding plants.

diseases.name: Spotted wilt virus
diseases.signs: Bronze rings, black streaks, stunted growth.
diseases.why: A virus spread by thrips.
diseases.fix: Remove infected plants. Control thrips.
diseases.prevent: Check new plants for thrips.

diseases.name: Cucumber mosaic virus
diseases.signs: Mottled yellow leaves, stunted and twisted growth.
diseases.why: A virus spread by aphids.
diseases.fix: Remove infected plants. Control aphids. Wash hands and tools.
diseases.prevent: Keep aphids under control.

diseases.name: Orchid virus
diseases.signs: Streaks, rings or black flecks on leaves and flowers.
diseases.why: A virus spread on cutting tools.
diseases.fix: Isolate the plant. Sterilise tools with flame or bleach. Bin it if it spreads.
diseases.prevent: Sterilise tools between orchids.

diseases.name: Rose mosaic
diseases.signs: Yellow wavy lines or patterns on rose leaves.
diseases.why: A virus from infected rootstock.
diseases.fix: No cure: the rose can still grow. Feed it well.
diseases.prevent: Buy from trusted growers.

diseases.name: Leaf gall
diseases.signs: Swollen, thick, pale leaves on azaleas and camellias.
diseases.why: A fungus in humid spring weather.
diseases.fix: Pick off galls before they turn white. Bin them.
diseases.prevent: Remove galls early each spring.

diseases.name: Slime mould
diseases.signs: Bright yellow or white blobs on soil or mulch.
diseases.why: A harmless organism in damp, rich material.
diseases.fix: Scoop it off and bin it. Let the surface dry.
diseases.prevent: Don't overwater and keep mulch thin.

diseases.name: Geranium bacterial blight
diseases.signs: V-shaped yellow wedges on leaves and wilting.
diseases.why: Bacteria spread by water and cuttings.
diseases.fix: Bin infected plants. Clean pots and tools.
diseases.prevent: Take cuttings only from healthy plants.

diseases.name: Iris leaf spot
diseases.signs: Brown oval spots with yellow edges on iris leaves.
diseases.why: A fungus in wet weather.
diseases.fix: Cut off spotted leaves. Clear debris in autumn.
diseases.prevent: Plant in sun with good drainage.

diseases.name: Fungus rings in pots
diseases.signs: Rings of mushrooms in large pots or beds.
diseases.why: Fungi feeding on organic matter.
diseases.fix: Remove mushrooms. Aerate and water deeply.
diseases.prevent: Use well-rotted compost.

diseases.name: Algal leaf spot
diseases.signs: Raised orange or green velvety spots on tough leaves.
diseases.why: Algae on leaves in warm, wet air.
diseases.fix: Remove spotted leaves. Keep leaves dry. Improve airflow.
diseases.prevent: Water at the base.

diseases.name: Chilling injury
diseases.signs: Pitted, dark or water-soaked leaves after a few cool nights.
diseases.why: Tropical plants kept below 10 °C.
diseases.fix: Move somewhere warmer. Trim dead parts once growth resumes.
diseases.prevent: Keep tropicals above 15 °C.

diseases.name: Frost damage
diseases.signs: Blackened, limp shoots after a frosty night.
diseases.why: Ice forming inside plant cells.
diseases.fix: Wait until spring to prune. Then cut back to healthy growth.
diseases.prevent: Bring tender plants in or cover them on frosty nights.

diseases.name: Salt damage
diseases.signs: Brown edges and dieback, crust on soil.
diseases.why: Too much fertiliser or salty water.
diseases.fix: Flush the pot with plenty of plain water. Pause feeding for a month.
diseases.prevent: Feed at half strength and flush every few months.

diseases.name: Weed killer damage
diseases.signs: Twisted, cupped, strappy new leaves.
diseases.why: Drift or residue from weed killer or treated manure.
diseases.fix: Remove affected growth. Water well. Replace soil if it came from treated manure.
diseases.prevent: Use trusted compost and don't spray near plants.

diseases.name: Wind damage
diseases.signs: Torn, browned leaves on the windy side.
diseases.why: Strong or cold wind on balconies.
diseases.fix: Trim torn leaves. Move to shelter or add a screen.
diseases.prevent: Group pots and use windbreaks.

deficiencies.name: Nitrogen
deficiencies.signs: Pale, evenly yellow older leaves; slow growth.
deficiencies.fix: A balanced feed in the growing season.

deficiencies.name: Phosphorus
deficiencies.signs: Dull, dark leaves with purple tints; poor roots and flowers.
deficiencies.fix: A balanced or bloom feed; check the soil isn't too cold.

deficiencies.name: Potassium
deficiencies.signs: Yellow or brown scorched edges on older leaves; few flowers.

deficiencies.name: Magnesium
deficiencies.signs: Yellow between the veins on older leaves.
deficiencies.fix: A feed with magnesium, or Epsom salts at 1 teaspoon per litre once.

deficiencies.name: Iron
deficiencies.signs: Yellow new leaves with green veins.
deficiencies.fix: Lower the pH (rainwater, ericaceous feed) and use chelated iron.

deficiencies.name: Calcium
deficiencies.signs: Distorted new growth; blossom end rot on tomatoes.
deficiencies.fix: Water evenly; most soils have calcium, but dry spells block it.

deficiencies.name: Sulphur
deficiencies.signs: Young leaves pale yellow all over, including veins.
deficiencies.fix: A complete feed with trace elements. Use compost in the mix.

deficiencies.name: Manganese
deficiencies.signs: Pale between veins on younger leaves, with tiny dead spots.
deficiencies.fix: Lower soil pH if it's chalky. Use a feed with trace elements.

deficiencies.name: Zinc
deficiencies.signs: Small, narrow new leaves, short gaps between them.
deficiencies.fix: Use a feed with trace elements. Check pH is not too high.

deficiencies.name: Boron
deficiencies.signs: Hollow stems, cracked fruit, dead growing tips.
deficiencies.fix: A feed with trace elements. Keep watering steady.

deficiencies.name: Copper
deficiencies.signs: Wilting new leaves, blue-green tint, dying tips.
deficiencies.fix: A feed with trace elements. Rarely needed in potting mix.

deficiencies.name: Molybdenum
deficiencies.signs: Pale, cupped leaves; whip-like leaves on brassicas.
deficiencies.fix: Raise pH in very acid soil. Use a feed with trace elements.

deficiencies.name: pH lockout
deficiencies.signs: Several hunger signs at once even though you feed.
deficiencies.fix: Check soil pH. Repot in fresh mix. Use rain or filtered water if tap water is very hard.

deficiencies.name: Salt burn
deficiencies.signs: Brown tips and edges, white crust, wilting after feeding.
deficiencies.fix: Flush the soil with plenty of water. Pause feeding. Then feed at half strength.

topics.title: Rooting cuttings in water
topics.intro: The easiest way to watch roots grow. Great for pothos, philodendron, tradescantia, monstera and coleus.

steps.title: Cut below a node
steps.detail: Snip a 10–15 cm stem just under a node, the little bump where a leaf meets the stem. That is where roots start.

steps.title: Strip the low leaves
steps.detail: Remove any leaf that would sit underwater, so it doesn't rot.

steps.title: Bright, not sunny
steps.detail: A clear glass on a bright windowsill out of direct midday sun is perfect.

steps.title: Fresh water weekly
steps.detail: Top up and swap the water every 5–7 days so it stays clear.

steps.title: Pot at 3–5 cm of roots
steps.detail: Move it to soil once roots are a few centimetres long and keep the soil a little moister than usual for two weeks.

topics.title: Rooting cuttings in soil
topics.intro: Cuttings rooted straight into soil skip the water-to-soil shock. Good for most herbs, begonias, succulents and woody plants.

steps.title: Take a healthy tip
steps.detail: Choose a non-flowering shoot with 2–3 nodes and cut just below the lowest one.

steps.title: Light, airy mix
steps.detail: Use half potting mix and half perlite or sand, lightly moist.

steps.title: Optional rooting powder
steps.detail: Dip the cut end in rooting hormone for tougher, woody stems.

steps.title: Keep the air humid
steps.detail: Cover loosely with a clear bag or bottle, opening it daily for fresh air.

steps.title: Tug test
steps.detail: After 3–6 weeks a gentle tug meets resistance: roots are in. Remove the cover slowly over a few days.

topics.title: Growing new plants from a single leaf
topics.intro: Some plants regrow a whole plant from one leaf: snake plant, ZZ, African violet, many succulents, begonia and peperomia.

steps.title: Pick a plump leaf
steps.detail: A healthy, mature leaf from the middle of the plant works best.

steps.title: Let succulent leaves callus
steps.detail: Leave succulent leaves on a dry plate for 2–4 days until the end seals over.

steps.title: Lay or insert
steps.detail: Rest succulent leaves on gritty mix; tuck violet and peperomia leaf stalks 1 cm into moist mix.

steps.title: Patience
steps.detail: Tiny plantlets appear after 4–12 weeks. Snake plant leaf sections can take months.

steps.title: Leave the mother leaf
steps.detail: Let it shrivel naturally; it feeds the baby until then.

topics.title: Dividing a crowded plant
topics.intro: Clumping plants make more of themselves. Split them when you repot: peace lily, calathea, ferns, snake plant, spider plant, aspidistra and many grasses.

steps.title: Spring is best
steps.detail: Divide at the start of the growing season so each piece recovers fast.

steps.title: Water the day before
steps.detail: Moist roots slide apart with less tearing.

steps.title: Tease apart
steps.detail: Ease the plant from its pot and pull clumps apart by hand, or cut through tough roots with a clean knife.

steps.title: Each piece needs roots and leaves
steps.detail: Aim for at least 3 shoots with a good root ball per division.

steps.title: Pot snugly
steps.detail: Use a pot just bigger than each root ball and keep out of strong sun for a week.

topics.title: Pups, runners and offsets
topics.intro: Many plants hand you babies: spider plant runners, aloe and haworthia pups, pilea offshoots, strawberry runners and bromeliad pups.

steps.title: Wait for size
steps.detail: Separate when the baby is about a third the size of its parent or has its own roots.

steps.title: Cut close
steps.detail: Use a clean blade to cut the connecting stem as close to the mother as you can.

steps.title: Pin runners
steps.detail: Spider plant and strawberry babies root fast if you pin them onto a pot of soil while still attached.

steps.title: Pot and settle
steps.detail: Small pot, light mix, bright indirect light, and water once the top is dry.

topics.title: Air layering a leggy plant
topics.intro: A way to root a branch while it is still on the plant. Ideal for tall rubber plants, monsteras and dracaenas that have lost their lower leaves.

steps.title: Choose a spot
steps.detail: Pick a node 20–30 cm below the tip.

steps.title: Wound gently
steps.detail: Make a small upward cut or scrape a ring of bark to encourage roots. For monstera, just wrap an aerial root and node.

steps.title: Wrap in moss
steps.detail: Pack damp sphagnum moss around it and wrap with clear plastic, tied at both ends.

steps.title: Keep it damp
steps.detail: Check weekly and add water so the moss never dries out.

steps.title: Cut and pot
steps.detail: When roots fill the moss, usually 4–8 weeks, cut below them and pot the new plant.

topics.title: Sowing seeds indoors
topics.intro: Herbs, chillies, tomatoes, flowers and even some houseplants start easily from seed.

steps.title: Fresh seed-starting mix
steps.detail: Use a fine, light mix. Garden soil is too heavy and can carry fungus.

steps.title: Sow at the right depth
steps.detail: A rough rule: cover seeds about twice their own thickness. Tiny seeds just press onto the surface.

steps.title: Warm and moist
steps.detail: Most seeds sprout best at 18–24 °C. Cover with a lid or clear bag until shoots appear.

steps.title: Light at once
steps.detail: Move seedlings to the brightest spot or under a grow light as soon as they appear, or they stretch.

steps.title: Thin and pot on
steps.detail: Keep the strongest seedling per cell and pot on when it has its first true leaves.

topics.title: Bottom watering
topics.intro: Letting a plant drink from below wets all the roots evenly and keeps leaves and crowns dry. Loved by African violets, calatheas, cacti and seedlings.

steps.title: Stand in water
steps.detail: Put the pot in a tray or bowl with 2–5 cm of room-temperature water.

steps.title: 10–30 minutes
steps.detail: Wait until the top of the soil feels damp.

steps.title: Drain fully
steps.detail: Lift it out and let extra water run away. Never leave it sitting.

steps.title: Top-water now and then
steps.detail: Every month or so, water from the top too, to flush out salts.

topics.title: Soaking a bone-dry plant
topics.intro: If soil has shrunk from the pot and water runs straight through, it has turned water-repellent.

steps.title: Sink it
steps.detail: Submerge the pot in a bucket until bubbles stop, about 10–20 minutes.

steps.title: Drain
steps.detail: Let it drip until no more water comes out.

steps.title: Loosen the surface
steps.detail: Gently fork the top crust so future water sinks in.

steps.title: Water a little more often
steps.detail: A plant that dried that far wants checking a bit sooner next time.

topics.title: Tap water, rain water and filtered water
topics.intro: Most plants are happy with tap water. A few are sensitive to salts, fluoride and chlorine: calatheas, marantas, dracaenas, spider plants, carnivorous plants and orchids.

steps.title: Let it stand
steps.detail: Leaving tap water out overnight lets chlorine escape and brings it to room temperature.

steps.title: Rain water is a treat
steps.detail: Collected rain water is soft and slightly acidic. Sensitive plants love it.

steps.title: Brown tips can be salts
steps.detail: Crispy brown tips on sensitive plants often mean mineral build-up. Flush the pot with plenty of water every month or two.

steps.title: Carnivores need pure water
steps.detail: Venus flytraps, sundews and pitcher plants need rain, distilled or reverse-osmosis water only.

steps.title: Avoid softened water
steps.detail: Water from a salt-based softener harms plants.

topics.title: Self-watering pots and wicks
topics.intro: A reservoir or cotton wick keeps soil evenly moist. Great for thirsty plants and holidays, less so for succulents.

steps.title: Good for
steps.detail: Ferns, peace lilies, African violets, herbs, tomatoes and fittonia.

steps.title: Not for
steps.detail: Cacti, succulents, snake plants and anything that likes to dry out.

steps.title: Use a chunky mix
steps.detail: Add perlite so the soil wicks without going soggy.

steps.title: Let it run dry sometimes
steps.detail: Let the reservoir empty for a couple of days now and then so roots get air.

topics.title: Reading thirst versus too much water
topics.intro: Both too little and too much water can make a plant droop. Here is how to tell.

steps.title: Thirsty
steps.detail: Soil dry and light, pot feels light, leaves soft and limp, crispy edges. Perks up within hours of a drink.

steps.title: Too wet
steps.detail: Soil damp and heavy, yellow lower leaves, mushy stems, fungus gnats, a sour smell. Watering makes it worse.

steps.title: The finger test
steps.detail: Push a finger 2–3 cm into the soil. Dry means water most plants; damp means wait.

steps.title: Lift the pot
steps.detail: Learn the weight of a just-watered pot. A much lighter pot is ready.

steps.title: A chopstick helps
steps.detail: Push a wooden skewer to the bottom and pull it out. Dark, damp soil clinging to it means wait.
