topics.title: Which window is which
topics.intro: The direction a window faces changes everything. In the Southern hemisphere, swap north and south.

steps.title: South-facing (north-facing down south)
steps.detail: The strongest light all day. Cacti, succulents, citrus and herbs love it. Pull tender plants a metre back in summer.

steps.title: West-facing
steps.detail: Gentle morning shade, then hot afternoon sun. Good for sun lovers; watch for scorch in summer.

steps.title: East-facing
steps.detail: Soft morning sun and bright shade later. The sweet spot for most tropical houseplants.

steps.title: North-facing (south-facing down south)
steps.detail: Even, gentle light with no direct sun. Ferns, calatheas, peace lilies, pothos and ZZ plants are happy.

steps.title: Distance matters
steps.detail: Light drops fast. One metre from a window can mean half the light, two metres a quarter.

topics.title: Grow lights, simply
topics.intro: A grow light lets you grow anywhere, even in a dark corner or through a grey winter.

steps.title: Full-spectrum white LED
steps.detail: A white full-spectrum LED looks normal and gives everything a plant needs. No purple glow needed.

steps.title: Distance
steps.detail: Hang it 20–40 cm above leafy plants and 15–25 cm above seedlings and herbs.

steps.title: 12–14 hours
steps.detail: Use a timer. Plants also need a dark rest each night.

steps.title: Signs it's too strong
steps.detail: Bleached or crispy spots on the top leaves: raise the light.

steps.title: Signs it's too weak
steps.detail: Long gaps between leaves and stems leaning toward the light: lower it or add hours.

topics.title: Reading light hunger and sunburn
topics.intro: Plants show you clearly when the light is wrong.

steps.title: Too little
steps.detail: Stretched stems, small new leaves, leaning hard to one side, variegation fading to plain green, no flowers.

steps.title: Too much
steps.detail: Bleached, yellow-white or brown crispy patches on the side facing the window.

steps.title: Turn the pot
steps.detail: A quarter turn every week or two keeps growth even.

steps.title: Move slowly
steps.detail: When moving a plant into much stronger light, do it over a week or two so leaves can adjust.

topics.title: Raising humidity that really helps
topics.intro: Calatheas, ferns, orchids and many tropicals like 50–60 % humidity. Heated rooms in winter often sit at 30 %.

steps.title: Group plants
steps.detail: Plants breathe out moisture. A cluster makes its own little humid pocket.

steps.title: Pebble tray
steps.detail: Stand pots on a tray of pebbles and water, with the pot base above the waterline.

steps.title: A humidifier is best
steps.detail: A small humidifier near the plants is the only thing that raises humidity a lot.

steps.title: Misting is brief
steps.detail: Misting lifts humidity for only a few minutes. It's nice, but not a fix on its own.

steps.title: Bathrooms and kitchens
steps.detail: A bright bathroom is a natural home for humidity lovers.

topics.title: Draughts, radiators and cold windows
topics.intro: Most houseplants like what we like: 16–26 °C, no sudden swings.

steps.title: Away from radiators
steps.detail: Heat sources dry leaves fast and cook roots. Keep plants a metre away.

steps.title: Cold glass
steps.detail: In winter, leaves touching cold glass can get damaged. Pull plants back on frosty nights.

steps.title: Draughts
steps.detail: Doors and leaky windows cause leaf drop, especially in fiddle leaf figs and crotons.

steps.title: AC blasts
steps.detail: Air conditioning is dry and cold. Keep plants out of the direct airflow.

steps.title: Night dip is good
steps.detail: A slightly cooler night helps many plants, and encourages orchids and Christmas cactus to flower.

topics.title: Settling in a new plant
topics.intro: A new plant has just left a perfect greenhouse. A few dropped leaves in the first weeks are normal.

steps.title: Check it over
steps.detail: Look under leaves and at the soil for pests before it joins the others.

steps.title: Quarantine 2 weeks
steps.detail: Keep it apart from your other plants for two weeks if you can.

steps.title: Don't repot yet
steps.detail: Let it adjust for 2–4 weeks unless it's root-bound or sitting in soggy soil.

steps.title: Find its spot and stay
steps.detail: Choose a spot that matches its light needs and resist moving it around.

steps.title: Water by the soil
steps.detail: Check the soil instead of following the label. Nursery soil can be very peaty and dry fast.

topics.title: When and how to repot
topics.intro: Most houseplants want a new pot every 1–3 years, in spring or early summer.

steps.title: Signs it's time
steps.detail: Roots poking out of the drainage holes, water rushing straight through, the plant toppling, or growth stalled.

steps.title: Only one size up
steps.detail: Choose a pot 2–5 cm wider. A huge pot holds too much wet soil.

steps.title: Holes are a must
steps.detail: Always use a pot with drainage holes, or a nursery pot inside a decorative one.

steps.title: Loosen the roots
steps.detail: Gently tease circling roots so they grow outward.

steps.title: Water and rest
steps.detail: Water well, then keep out of strong sun for a week. Hold the fertiliser for a month.

topics.title: Pruning and pinching
topics.intro: Pruning keeps plants full, healthy and the size you want.

steps.title: Pinch for bushiness
steps.detail: Pinch off the growing tip of herbs, coleus, pothos and basil to make two shoots grow.

steps.title: Cut above a node
steps.detail: Always cut just above a leaf joint. That's where new growth starts.

steps.title: Clean blades
steps.detail: Wipe scissors with alcohol between plants to avoid spreading disease.

steps.title: Remove the dead
steps.detail: Yellow, brown or damaged leaves can be cut off at the base any time.

steps.title: Big cuts in spring
steps.detail: Save hard pruning for the start of the growing season.

topics.title: Cleaning leaves
topics.intro: Dust blocks light and hides pests. Clean leaves breathe and grow better.

steps.title: Damp cloth
steps.detail: Wipe big leaves with a soft damp cloth, supporting each leaf from below.

steps.title: Shower
steps.detail: Small or bushy plants can have a lukewarm shower. Let them drip dry out of the sun.

steps.title: Soft brush
steps.detail: Fuzzy leaves (African violets, some begonias) hate water: use a soft paintbrush.

steps.title: Skip leaf shine
steps.detail: Shine products can clog leaf pores. Plain water is best.

steps.title: Check for pests
steps.detail: Cleaning time is the best time to spot spider mites and mealybugs.

topics.title: Winter rest and dormancy
topics.intro: Many plants slow down in the darker months. That isn't a problem; it's a rest.

steps.title: Water less
steps.detail: Soil dries slower in winter. Check before watering, and expect gaps up to twice as long.

steps.title: Stop feeding
steps.detail: Pause fertiliser from late autumn until new growth starts in spring.

steps.title: Some go fully dormant
steps.detail: Caladiums, some begonias, bulbs and many cacti go dormant. Keep them cool and nearly dry.

steps.title: Cacti like it cool
steps.detail: A cool, dry, bright winter helps many cacti flower next spring.

steps.title: Wake up gently
steps.detail: When new growth appears, resume normal watering and start feeding at half strength.

topics.title: Going away: keeping plants alive
topics.intro: A little planning keeps plants happy for one to three weeks.

steps.title: Water well before
steps.detail: Give everything a deep drink the day before you leave.

steps.title: Pull back from windows
steps.detail: Move plants a little out of strong sun so they drink slower.

steps.title: Group them
steps.detail: Grouped plants keep each other humid.

steps.title: Bathtub trick
steps.detail: For a week or two, stand pots on a damp towel in a bath with a few centimetres of water.

steps.title: Wicks and bottles
steps.detail: A cotton wick from a water jug or an upturned bottle spike keeps thirsty plants going.

steps.title: Succulents are fine
steps.detail: Cacti and succulents can go two to four weeks with no help.

topics.title: Feeding without fuss
topics.intro: Plants make their own food from light. Fertiliser is more like vitamins: a little, in the growing season.

steps.title: Spring to autumn
steps.detail: Feed when the plant is actively growing. Pause in winter.

steps.title: Half strength
steps.detail: Most houseplants do best on fertiliser at half the strength on the bottle.

steps.title: Moist soil first
steps.detail: Never feed bone-dry soil. Water first, or feed with the watering.

steps.title: Signs of too much
steps.detail: A white crust on the soil, brown leaf tips, or sudden wilting after feeding. Flush with plenty of water.

steps.title: Fresh soil feeds
steps.detail: A newly repotted plant has food in its soil. Wait 4–6 weeks.

topics.title: Keeping pets and plants friends
topics.intro: Some common houseplants upset cats and dogs if chewed. Most cause mouth irritation or tummy trouble; lilies are serious for cats.

steps.title: Lilies and cats
steps.detail: True lilies (Lilium) and daylilies (Hemerocallis) can cause kidney failure in cats, even from pollen or vase water. Keep them out of homes with cats.

steps.title: Common irritants
steps.detail: Pothos, philodendron, monstera, dieffenbachia, peace lily, ZZ and aloe can cause drooling, mouth pain or vomiting.

steps.title: Pet-safe picks
steps.detail: Spider plant, calathea, parlour palm, Boston fern, peperomia, African violet, haworthia and most herbs are considered non-toxic.

steps.title: Place smart
steps.detail: Hanging baskets and high shelves keep tempting plants out of reach.

steps.title: If they chew
steps.detail: Rinse their mouth, note the plant, and call your vet or a pet poison line straight away.

topics.title: Plants and little children
topics.intro: Toddlers taste everything. Most houseplants only cause mild irritation, but a few are worth keeping out of reach.

steps.title: Higher shelves
steps.detail: Keep irritating plants (dieffenbachia, pothos, philodendron, euphorbias with milky sap) up high.

steps.title: Berries and seeds
steps.detail: Remove berries from plants like Jerusalem cherry and avoid castor bean entirely.

steps.title: Wash hands
steps.detail: Wash hands after handling euphorbias and plants with sap.

steps.title: If swallowed
steps.detail: Wipe the mouth, keep a piece of the plant, and call your local poison centre.

topics.title: Harvesting herbs so they keep giving
topics.intro: Regular picking makes herbs bushier and tastier.

steps.title: Pick from the top
steps.detail: Snip basil, mint and oregano just above a pair of leaves; two new shoots grow.

steps.title: Never more than a third
steps.detail: Leave at least two-thirds of the plant to keep growing.

steps.title: Stop the flowers
steps.detail: Pinch flower buds off basil, mint and coriander to keep leaves coming.

steps.title: Morning is tastiest
steps.detail: Harvest in the morning, after the dew dries, when oils are strongest.

steps.title: Woody herbs
steps.detail: Rosemary, thyme and sage: cut soft green tips, not old wood.

topics.title: Growing from kitchen scraps
topics.intro: Some kitchen leftovers regrow happily on a windowsill.

steps.title: Spring onions
steps.detail: Stand the white roots in a little water. New green shoots in days.

steps.title: Lettuce and celery bases
steps.detail: Sit the base in shallow water for fresh leaves, then pot up.

steps.title: Avocado
steps.detail: Suspend the stone half in water with toothpicks, pointy end up. Roots in 4–8 weeks.

steps.title: Ginger and turmeric
steps.detail: Plant a plump piece with visible buds just under moist soil in a warm spot.

steps.title: Pineapple top
steps.detail: Twist off the crown, strip the lowest leaves, dry a day, then root in water or gritty soil.

topics.title: Plant myths, gently busted
topics.intro: A few popular ideas that don't hold up.

steps.title: Gravel at the bottom helps drainage
steps.detail: It actually raises the wet layer into the root zone. Use a free-draining mix and a pot with holes instead.

steps.title: Ice cubes are a good way to water
steps.detail: They work for some orchids, but cold water and uneven wetting suit few plants. Room-temperature water is better.

steps.title: Houseplants purify the air of a room
steps.detail: Lab studies were in sealed chambers. In a real home, normal ventilation does far more. Plants still make rooms nicer.

steps.title: Yellow leaves always mean overwatering
steps.detail: Old leaves yellow naturally, and underwatering, low light and hunger all cause yellowing too.

steps.title: Misting fixes dry air
steps.detail: Misting raises humidity only for minutes. A humidifier or grouping plants helps much more.

steps.title: Bigger pots grow bigger plants faster
steps.detail: Too much wet soil around small roots leads to rot. One size up at a time.

steps.title: Talking to plants helps
steps.detail: Plants don't hear words, but people who talk to their plants check on them more, and that does help.

topics.title: Pots without holes
topics.intro: Drainage holes are the single biggest thing that stops root rot.

steps.title: Use a cachepot
steps.detail: Keep the plant in a plastic nursery pot with holes inside the pretty pot.

steps.title: Empty the saucer
steps.detail: Tip out water that collects 15 minutes after watering.

steps.title: Drill it
steps.detail: Ceramic pots can be drilled with a tile bit and a little water to cool it.

steps.title: If you must
steps.detail: Only for very experienced waterers: measure water carefully and check soil often.

topics.title: Refreshing tired soil
topics.intro: Soil compacts and loses food over time.

steps.title: Top dress
steps.detail: Scrape off the top 2–3 cm and replace with fresh mix or a little worm compost.

steps.title: Aerate
steps.detail: Gently poke a chopstick into compacted soil to let air and water in.

steps.title: Flush salts
steps.detail: Water slowly with plenty of water until it runs freely out, every few months.

steps.title: Replace yearly-ish
steps.detail: Peat-based mixes break down. A full repot every 2–3 years keeps roots happy.

topics.title: Getting plants to flower again
topics.intro: Many plants need a seasonal signal to bloom again.

steps.title: Orchids (Phalaenopsis)
steps.detail: A few weeks of cooler nights (around 15 °C) in autumn triggers a new spike. Keep in bright, indirect light.

steps.title: Christmas and Thanksgiving cactus
steps.detail: Long, dark nights (12–14 hours) and cooler temps for 6 weeks in autumn, with less water.

steps.title: Poinsettia
steps.detail: Needs 14 hours of total darkness nightly for about 8 weeks from autumn to colour up.

steps.title: Peace lily
steps.detail: More light is usually the answer, plus a spring feed.

steps.title: Amaryllis
steps.detail: After flowering, keep the leaves growing all summer, then rest it dry for 8–10 weeks before restarting.

topics.title: Balcony and patio growing
topics.intro: Balconies are windier, sunnier and dry faster than you'd think.

steps.title: Wind
steps.detail: Choose sturdy plants and heavier pots. Grasses, rosemary, lavender and succulents cope well.

steps.title: Pots dry fast
steps.detail: Outdoor pots can need water daily in summer. Bigger pots and mulch help.

steps.title: Weight
steps.detail: Large wet pots are heavy. Use lightweight pots and mixes on high balconies.

steps.title: Bring in tropicals
steps.detail: Most houseplants enjoy summer outside in shade, but bring them in before nights drop below 10 °C.

steps.title: Pests on return
steps.detail: Check and rinse plants for pests before they come back indoors.

topics.title: Protecting plants from frost
topics.intro: A frost can damage tender plants overnight.

steps.title: Watch the forecast
steps.detail: Below about 2 °C at night means frost is possible on clear, still nights.

steps.title: Move pots in
steps.detail: Bring tender pots into a shed, garage or indoors overnight.

steps.title: Cover up
steps.detail: Drape fleece or an old sheet over plants in the evening; remove in the morning. Avoid plastic touching leaves.

steps.title: Water in the morning
steps.detail: Moist soil holds more heat than dry, but avoid watering at night.

steps.title: Wait to prune
steps.detail: Leave frost-damaged growth until spring; it protects the buds beneath.

topics.title: Helping plants through a heatwave
topics.intro: Very hot days stress plants in pots most.

steps.title: Water early
steps.detail: Water deeply in the early morning, not in the midday sun.

steps.title: Shade
steps.detail: Move pots to shade or rig up a shade cloth for the hottest hours.

steps.title: Mulch
steps.detail: A layer of bark, gravel or straw keeps roots cooler and soil moist.

steps.title: No feeding or repotting
steps.detail: Wait until the heat passes.

steps.title: Indoor plants too
steps.detail: Pull plants back from hot windows and draw sheer curtains.

topics.title: Getting rid of fungus gnats
topics.intro: Tiny black flies around the soil are fungus gnats. Their larvae live in damp soil.

steps.title: Let the top dry
steps.detail: Let the top 3–5 cm of soil dry between waterings. Larvae need moisture.

steps.title: Yellow sticky traps
steps.detail: Catch the adults so they can't lay more eggs.

steps.title: Bottom water
steps.detail: Watering from below keeps the surface drier.

steps.title: BTI
steps.detail: Mosquito bits (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) soaked in water kill larvae safely.

steps.title: Top layer of sand
steps.detail: A thin layer of sand or grit on top makes the soil less inviting.

topics.title: White fuzz or mould on soil
topics.intro: A white fluffy layer on soil is usually harmless saprophytic mould, but it means things are too damp.

steps.title: Scrape it off
steps.detail: Remove the top layer of mould and soil.

steps.title: More air
steps.detail: Improve airflow and water less often.

steps.title: Light helps
steps.detail: More light dries soil faster and discourages mould.

steps.title: Cinnamon
steps.detail: A sprinkle of cinnamon on the surface is a gentle natural antifungal.

topics.title: Fixing a leggy, stretched plant
topics.intro: Long bare stems mean the plant has been reaching for light.

steps.title: More light first
steps.detail: Move it closer to a window or add a grow light, or new growth stretches too.

steps.title: Cut back
steps.detail: Prune stems just above a node to encourage branching lower down.

steps.title: Root the tips
steps.detail: Use the cut tops as cuttings and plant them back in the same pot for a fuller look.

steps.title: Rotate
steps.detail: Turn the pot regularly so all sides get light.

topics.title: How to repot
topics.intro: Spring is the best time. Go up just one pot size.

steps.title: Water the day before
steps.detail: Moist roots slide out easier and suffer less.

steps.title: Ease it out
steps.detail: Tip the pot, support the base and slide the plant out. Loosen circling roots.

steps.title: Settle it in
steps.detail: Set it at the same depth in fresh mix, firm gently and water well.

topics.title: Choosing pot size
topics.intro: A pot too big stays wet; too small dries daily.

steps.title: Measure the roots
steps.detail: Pick a pot 2 to 5 cm wider than the rootball.

steps.title: Check the holes
steps.detail: Always use a pot with drainage holes.

steps.title: Match the plant
steps.detail: Fast growers can go up a bit more; succulents prefer snug.

topics.title: Terracotta vs plastic
topics.intro: The pot changes how fast the soil dries.

steps.title: Terracotta
steps.detail: Breathes and dries fast. Great for succulents and overwaterers.

steps.title: Plastic
steps.detail: Holds moisture longer. Good for ferns and thirsty plants.

steps.title: Glazed ceramic
steps.detail: Like plastic, but heavier. Check it has a hole.

topics.title: Using self-watering pots
topics.intro: Handy, but not for every plant.

steps.title: Fill the reservoir
steps.detail: Top up when the gauge or reservoir is empty.

steps.title: Let it run dry
steps.detail: Let the reservoir empty for a few days between fills.

steps.title: Skip for succulents
steps.detail: Cacti and succulents rot in constant moisture.

topics.title: Pots without holes
topics.intro: Water has nowhere to go, so roots sit wet.

steps.title: Use as a cover
steps.detail: Keep the plant in a plastic pot with holes inside it.

steps.title: Drill a hole
steps.detail: A diamond bit drills ceramics with care and water.

steps.title: Skip the gravel
steps.detail: Gravel at the bottom doesn't fix drainage.

topics.title: The finger test
topics.intro: The simplest way to know when to water.

steps.title: Push in a finger

crops.name: Tomato
crops.start: Sow indoors 6–8 weeks before your last frost; plant out when nights stay above 10 °C.
crops.tip: Water deeply and evenly to prevent cracked fruit and blossom-end rot. Pinch side shoots on tall (cordon) types.

crops.name: Cherry tomato
crops.start: Sow indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost.
crops.tip: Tumbling varieties are perfect for hanging baskets and balcony rails.

crops.name: Chilli pepper
crops.start: Sow indoors 8–10 weeks before last frost, ideally on a warm mat at 25 °C.
crops.tip: Chillies love warmth and do brilliantly on a sunny windowsill. A little stress near ripening makes them hotter.

crops.name: Sweet pepper
crops.start: Sow indoors 8–10 weeks before last frost.
crops.tip: Pick the first fruits green to encourage more to set.

crops.name: Aubergine
crops.start: Sow indoors 8–10 weeks before last frost.
crops.tip: Needs a long, hot season. A greenhouse or very sunny wall helps in cooler climates.

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.start: Sow indoors 3–4 weeks before last frost or outside once soil is 18 °C.
crops.tip: Give climbing types a trellis. Pick often; overgrown fruit slows the plant.

crops.name: Courgette
crops.start: Sow indoors 3–4 weeks before last frost or direct after frost.
crops.tip: One plant feeds a family. Pick at 15–20 cm, and check daily in summer.

crops.name: Pumpkin and winter squash
crops.start: Sow indoors 3–4 weeks before last frost.
crops.tip: Cure harvested fruit in the sun for 1–2 weeks so they keep for months.

crops.name: Dwarf French beans
crops.start: Sow direct after last frost when soil is above 12 °C.
crops.tip: Pick young and often for tender pods and a longer harvest.

crops.name: Runner and climbing beans
crops.start: Sow direct after last frost, or indoors 3 weeks earlier.
crops.tip: Grow up a wigwam of canes. Mist the flowers in hot, dry spells to help pods set.

crops.name: Peas
crops.start: Sow direct in early spring as soon as soil can be worked; peas like it cool.
crops.tip: Pea shoots grown on a windowsill are a quick, sweet harvest in 2–3 weeks.

crops.name: Lettuce
crops.start: Sow little and often from early spring to late summer.
crops.tip: Bolts in heat. Grow in light shade in summer and keep moist. Cut-and-come-again leaves regrow several times.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.start: Sow in early spring or late summer; it bolts in long hot days.
crops.tip: A cool-season favourite. Try perpetual spinach (chard) for summer.

crops.name: Swiss chard
crops.start: Sow spring to midsummer.
crops.tip: Pick outer leaves and it keeps going for a year. Colourful stems look lovely in pots.

crops.name: Kale
crops.start: Sow spring to early summer; frost sweetens the leaves.
crops.tip: Cover with fine mesh against cabbage white caterpillars.

crops.name: Radish
crops.start: Sow direct every 2 weeks from spring to autumn.
crops.tip: The fastest crop there is. Keep evenly moist or they go woody and hot.

crops.name: Carrot
crops.start: Sow direct from spring to midsummer.
crops.tip: Round or short varieties grow well in pots. Sow thinly to avoid thinning, which attracts carrot fly.

crops.name: Beetroot
crops.start: Sow direct from spring to midsummer.
crops.tip: Each seed is a cluster; thin to one seedling. Young leaves are great in salads.

crops.name: Onion
crops.start: Plant sets in early spring or autumn; sow seed indoors late winter.
crops.tip: Stop watering once the tops fall over, then let them dry before storing.

crops.name: Spring onion
crops.start: Sow little and often from spring to late summer.
crops.tip: Regrows from the white roots in a glass of water.

crops.name: Garlic
crops.start: Plant cloves in autumn for a summer harvest; most need a cold spell.
crops.tip: Plant pointy end up, 5 cm deep. Harvest when the lower third of leaves turn yellow.

crops.name: Potato
crops.start: Plant chitted tubers in spring after the worst frosts.
crops.tip: Grow in a deep bag; add compost over the shoots as they grow (earthing up) for more tubers.

crops.name: Sweet potato
crops.start: Root slips in water 6–8 weeks before planting out into warm soil.
crops.tip: A trailing, pretty foliage plant indoors too. Leaves are edible.

crops.name: Strawberry
crops.start: Plant runners in spring or late summer.
crops.harvestDays: fruits next summer; everbearers same year
crops.tip: Mulch with straw to keep fruit clean. Replace plants every 3 years.

crops.name: Blueberry
crops.start: Plant any time in mild weather in ericaceous (acid) compost.
crops.tip: Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5–5.5. Water with rain water. Two varieties crop better.

crops.name: Sweet corn
crops.start: Sow indoors 3–4 weeks before last frost in deep cells, or direct after frost.
crops.tip: Plant in a block, not a row, so the wind pollinates the cobs.

crops.name: Pak choi
crops.start: Sow late summer for best results; spring sowings bolt.
crops.tip: Harvest baby leaves in 3 weeks.

crops.name: Rocket
crops.start: Sow little and often spring to autumn.
crops.tip: Peppery leaves get hotter in heat and dry soil.

crops.name: Microgreens
crops.start: Sow any time indoors on a shallow tray.
crops.tip: Pea, radish, sunflower, broccoli and mustard are easiest. Cut just above the soil.

crops.name: Basil
crops.start: Sow indoors any time it's warm, or outside when nights stay above 12 °C.
crops.tip: Water at the base in the morning. Pinch tops and flowers. Hates cold and wet.

crops.name: Parsley
crops.start: Sow spring to summer; soak seed overnight, it's slow to sprout.
crops.tip: A biennial: it flowers and fades in its second year.

crops.name: Coriander
crops.start: Sow direct every 3 weeks; it dislikes transplanting.
crops.tip: Bolts fast in heat. Let some flower: seeds are delicious and attract hoverflies.

crops.name: Mint
crops.start: Plant root cuttings any time in the growing season.
crops.tip: Always grow in its own pot: it spreads everywhere in beds.

crops.name: Chives
crops.start: Sow spring or divide clumps.
crops.tip: Cut right down to 3 cm; it regrows fast. Purple flowers are edible.

crops.name: Thyme
crops.start: Buy a plant or root cuttings in spring.
crops.tip: Gritty, free-draining soil and little water. Trim after flowering.

crops.name: Rosemary
crops.start: Root cuttings in spring or summer.
crops.tip: Hates wet roots in winter. Terracotta and gritty mix.

crops.name: Oregano
crops.start: Sow spring indoors or divide clumps.
crops.tip: Flavour is strongest just before flowering.

crops.name: Dill
crops.start: Sow direct every 3 weeks.
crops.tip: Tall and wispy; attracts beneficial insects.

crops.name: Lemongrass
crops.start: Root shop-bought stalks in water, then pot.
crops.tip: Bring indoors below 5 °C. Cut stalks at the base.

crops.name: Ginger
crops.start: Plant plump pieces with buds in spring indoors.
crops.tip: Grows lush foliage. Harvest small pieces from the edge after 4 months.

crops.name: Lemon tree
crops.start: Buy a grafted plant; plant in spring.
crops.harvestDays: fruits in 1–3 years on grafted plants
crops.tip: Citrus food in summer, water when the top 3 cm dries. Bring in before frost.

crops.name: Fig tree
crops.start: Plant in spring; restrict roots in a pot for more fruit.
crops.tip: Pinch new shoots to 5 leaves in early summer for more fruit.

crops.name: Olive tree
crops.start: Plant in spring in gritty, free-draining mix.
crops.tip: Very drought tolerant once settled. Hates soggy winters.

families.name: Araceae
families.traits: Big leaves from a hooded flower (spathe and spadix). Many climb with aerial roots, and many split or fenestrate leaves as they mature.
families.care: Chunky, airy mix, bright indirect light, water when the top third dries. A moss pole makes climbers grow bigger leaves.
families.toxic: Most contain calcium oxalate crystals that sting the mouth of pets and people.

families.name: Marantaceae
families.traits: Patterned leaves that fold up at night and open at dawn.
families.care: Steady moisture, high humidity, soft or rain water, no direct sun. Brown tips mean dry air or salty water.
families.toxic: Non-toxic to cats and dogs.

families.name: Cactaceae
families.traits: Swollen stems that store water, spines from little pads called areoles. Almost all from the Americas.
families.care: Brightest light, gritty mix, water thoroughly then let dry fully. Cool, dry winter rest for flowers.
families.toxic: Mostly non-toxic; the spines are the danger.

families.name: Crassulaceae
families.traits: Fleshy succulent leaves, often in rosettes, that store water.
families.care: Bright sun, gritty mix, soak and dry. Leaves root easily.
families.toxic: Jade and kalanchoe are mildly toxic to pets; echeveria and sempervivum are considered safe.

families.name: Asparagaceae
families.traits: A varied family of tough plants: rosettes, swords and fern-like fronds.
families.care: Mostly very forgiving: moderate light, let soil dry partly.
families.toxic: Snake plant and dracaena mildly irritating; spider plant is safe.

families.name: Moraceae
families.traits: Woody plants with milky latex sap.
families.care: Bright light, steady routine; they drop leaves when moved or chilled.
families.toxic: Ficus sap irritates skin and is mildly toxic if chewed.

families.name: Orchidaceae
families.traits: The largest flowering plant family. Many grow on trees, holding on with silvery aerial roots.
families.care: Bark mix, bright indirect light, water when roots turn silver. Cooler nights trigger flowers.
families.toxic: Phalaenopsis is non-toxic.

families.name: Bromeliaceae
families.traits: Rosettes that often hold water in a central cup; many are air plants.
families.care: Bright indirect light, water in the cup or soak air plants, little soil. The mother flowers once then makes pups.
families.toxic: Non-toxic.

families.name: Arecaceae
families.traits: Single growing points: cut the top and the stem stops.
families.care: Bright indirect light, steady moisture, never cut green fronds. Brown tips from dry air or salts.
families.toxic: Most indoor palms are pet-safe; sago 'palm' is not a palm and is very toxic.

families.name: Gesneriaceae
families.traits: Soft, often furry leaves and long-blooming flowers.
families.care: Bright indirect light, bottom water with tepid water, keep leaves dry.
families.toxic: Non-toxic.

families.name: Lamiaceae
families.traits: Square stems, opposite leaves and aromatic oils.
families.care: Most herbs here want sun and good drainage; pinch tips to keep bushy.
families.toxic: Mostly safe; pennyroyal is toxic.

families.name: Solanaceae
families.traits: Fruiting crops and ornamentals; leaves and green fruit often toxic.
families.care: Full sun, warmth, steady water and potassium-rich feed when fruiting.
families.toxic: Leaves and stems of tomato, potato and pepper are toxic to pets.

families.name: Asteraceae
families.traits: What looks like one flower is many tiny flowers packed together.
families.care: Mostly sun lovers with moderate water.
families.toxic: Chrysanthemums are toxic to pets; most others mild.

families.name: Apocynaceae
families.traits: Often milky sap; includes waxy flowers and star-shaped succulents.
families.care: Bright light, let dry between waters.
families.toxic: Many are toxic: oleander and adenium seriously so.

families.name: Begoniaceae
families.traits: Lopsided leaves, often silver-spotted or glittering.
families.care: Bright indirect light, let the top dry, keep leaves dry, good airflow against mildew.
families.toxic: Toxic to pets, especially the tubers.

families.name: Euphorbiaceae
families.traits: Milky sap that irritates skin and eyes; flowers often hidden in coloured bracts.
families.care: Mostly bright light and dry soil; wear gloves when pruning.
families.toxic: Sap is irritating; keep from pets and children.

families.name: Araliaceae
families.traits: Hand-shaped or divided leaves, often variegated.
families.care: Bright indirect light, even moisture; mist against spider mites.
families.toxic: Mildly toxic.

families.name: Piperaceae
families.traits: Thick, often succulent leaves on compact plants.
families.care: Bright indirect light, let dry halfway; easy from leaf cuttings.
families.toxic: Non-toxic.

families.name: Ferns
families.traits: No flowers or seeds: ferns spread by spores on the underside of fronds (those brown dots are normal).
families.care: Even moisture, high humidity, no direct sun.
families.toxic: Most true ferns are pet-safe; asparagus fern is not a fern and is toxic.

families.name: Rutaceae
families.traits: Aromatic leaves with oil glands; scented flowers.
families.care: Full sun, citrus feed, water when top dries, no cold draughts.
families.toxic: Mildly toxic to pets.

remedies.name: Gentle soap spray
remedies.recipe: 1 teaspoon (5 ml) pure liquid castile soap in 1 litre of lukewarm water.
remedies.how: Spray every surface, especially under leaves, until dripping. Repeat every 5–7 days for 3 weeks.
remedies.caution: Test on one leaf first. Avoid dish soaps with degreasers. Don't spray in hot sun.

remedies.forWhat: mealybugs, scale, spider mites, thrips, mildew
remedies.recipe: 1 teaspoon (5 ml) cold-pressed neem oil plus ½ teaspoon castile soap in 1 litre of warm water. Shake well.
remedies.how: Spray all surfaces in the evening. Repeat weekly for a month.
remedies.caution: Can mark tender leaves and smells strong. Mix fresh each time. Not near fish tanks.

remedies.name: Rubbing alcohol dab
remedies.recipe: 70 % isopropyl alcohol on a cotton bud.
remedies.how: Dab each bug directly; they dissolve on contact. Check every few days.
remedies.caution: Test on one leaf first. Not on fuzzy or very thin leaves.

remedies.name: Shower blast
remedies.recipe: Lukewarm water from a shower head.
remedies.how: Rinse leaves top and bottom, covering the soil with a bag. Repeat weekly.
remedies.caution: Let the plant drip dry out of sun.

remedies.name: Yellow sticky traps
remedies.recipe: Yellow sticky cards.
remedies.how: Stick one in the soil or hang near the plant. Change when full.
remedies.caution: Keep away from pets' fur.

remedies.name: Mosquito bits (BTI) water
remedies.recipe: 1 tablespoon of BTI granules steeped in 4 litres of water for 30 minutes.
remedies.how: Strain and water the soil with it for 3 waterings in a row.
remedies.caution: Safe for people, pets and plants.

remedies.name: Cinnamon dust
remedies.forWhat: mould on soil, damping off, cut stems
remedies.recipe: Ground cinnamon.
remedies.how: Sprinkle thinly on the soil surface or dab on fresh cuts.
remedies.caution: A gentle aid, not a cure for rot.

remedies.name: Hydrogen peroxide drench
remedies.forWhat: root rot, fungus gnat larvae, stale soil
remedies.recipe: 1 part 3 % hydrogen peroxide to 4 parts water.
remedies.how: Water through the soil once; it fizzes as it works.
remedies.caution: Only the 3 % kind. Once, not routinely: it also kills good microbes.

remedies.name: Milk spray for mildew
remedies.recipe: 1 part milk to 9 parts water.
remedies.how: Spray leaves in morning sun weekly.
remedies.caution: Best as prevention or early on.

remedies.name: Bicarbonate spray
remedies.recipe: 1 teaspoon baking soda and ½ teaspoon castile soap in 1 litre of water.
remedies.how: Spray affected leaves weekly.
remedies.caution: Too much burns leaves. Not for frequent use.

remedies.name: Garlic spray
remedies.recipe: 2 crushed cloves steeped overnight in 1 litre of water, strained, plus a drop of soap.
remedies.how: Spray leaves every few days.
remedies.caution: Smells; best outdoors.

remedies.name: Diatomaceous earth
remedies.recipe: Food-grade diatomaceous earth.
remedies.how: Dust a thin layer on dry soil; reapply after watering.
remedies.caution: Don't breathe the dust. Only works dry.

remedies.name: Copper tape
remedies.recipe: Copper tape.
remedies.how: Ring the rim of pots.
remedies.caution: Keep it clean so it keeps working.

remedies.name: Beneficial insects
remedies.recipe: Ladybirds, lacewings, predatory mites (Phytoseiulus, Amblyseius).
remedies.how: Release in the evening onto infested plants; best in greenhouses or a sunroom.
remedies.caution: Stop all sprays first, they kill helpers too.

remedies.name: Quarantine and clean-up
remedies.recipe: A separate room or bag, clean scissors, fresh soil.
remedies.how: Isolate the plant, remove the worst leaves, wipe the pot and shelf, then treat.
remedies.caution: Check neighbours too: pests travel.

remedies.name: Horticultural oil
remedies.recipe: Use a ready-made horticultural oil spray.
remedies.how: Coat leaves and stems fully. Repeat every 7 to 10 days, 3 times.
remedies.caution: Not in sun or heat over 30 °C. Test on one leaf first. Not for hairy-leaved plants.

remedies.name: Insecticidal soap
remedies.recipe: Buy a ready-to-use insecticidal soap.
remedies.how: Spray all surfaces until wet. Repeat weekly for 3 weeks.
remedies.caution: Rinse leaves after a few hours on sensitive plants.

remedies.name: Predatory mites
remedies.recipe: Buy sachets of Phytoseiulus or Amblyseius mites.
remedies.how: Hang sachets on the plant and keep humidity up.
remedies.caution: Don't spray any pesticide while they work.

remedies.name: Ladybirds and lacewings
remedies.recipe: Buy larvae or welcome wild ones.
remedies.how: Release at dusk near colonies.
remedies.caution: Works best outdoors or in greenhouses.

remedies.name: Beneficial nematodes
remedies.forWhat: fungus gnat larvae, vine weevil grubs
remedies.recipe: Buy Steinernema nematodes and mix with water as directed.
remedies.how: Water onto moist soil in the evening.
remedies.caution: Use within the date. Soil must stay moist and above 10 °C.

remedies.name: Yellow sticky traps
remedies.recipe: Yellow sticky cards.
remedies.how: Push into the soil or hang near the plant. Replace when full.
remedies.caution: Keep away from pets and hair.

remedies.name: Blue sticky traps
remedies.recipe: Blue sticky cards.
remedies.how: Hang at plant height. Check weekly to see if thrips are present.
remedies.caution: They monitor more than they cure.

remedies.name: Handheld vacuum
remedies.recipe: A small handheld vacuum.
remedies.how: Gently hover over leaves to lift adults. Empty outside.
remedies.caution: Never touch leaves with the nozzle.

remedies.name: Strong water spray
remedies.recipe: A hose or shower.
remedies.how: Spray leaf undersides firmly. Repeat every 3 days.
remedies.caution: Support stems; let leaves dry in good light.

remedies.name: Plastic bag quarantine
remedies.recipe: A clear plastic bag big enough for the plant.
remedies.how: Cover for a day to trap flying pests, then inspect.
remedies.caution: Not in sun: it overheats fast.

remedies.name: Sand top layer
remedies.recipe: 1 to 2 cm of coarse sand or grit.
remedies.how: Spread over dry soil so gnats can't lay eggs.
remedies.caution: Check moisture with a finger or chopstick.

remedies.name: Potato slice test
remedies.recipe: A raw potato slice.
remedies.how: Lay it on the soil for 2 days and look underneath for larvae.
remedies.caution: For checking only, not a cure.

remedies.name: Beer trap
remedies.recipe: A shallow dish of cheap beer.
remedies.how: Sink it to rim level near plants. Empty every morning.
remedies.caution: Keep away from pets.

remedies.name: Copper tape
remedies.recipe: Copper tape for pots.
remedies.how: Stick a band around the pot rim.
remedies.caution: Keep it clean so it works.

remedies.name: Sulphur dust
remedies.recipe: Garden sulphur powder.
remedies.how: Dust cut surfaces or lightly dust leaves.
remedies.caution: Not with oils within 2 weeks. Wear a mask.

remedies.name: Cinnamon on cuts
remedies.forWhat: cut stems, root trimming, damping off
remedies.recipe: Ground cinnamon from the kitchen.
remedies.how: Dust fresh cuts and let them dry.
remedies.caution: A mild help, not a strong fungicide.

remedies.name: Peroxide root rinse
remedies.recipe: 1 part 3% hydrogen peroxide in 4 parts water.
remedies.how: Rinse cleaned roots once before repotting.
remedies.caution: Never stronger. Don't use often.

remedies.name: Alcohol swab
remedies.recipe: 70% rubbing alcohol on a cotton bud.
remedies.how: Dab each insect. Repeat every few days.
remedies.caution: Test on one leaf. Keep away from flames.

remedies.name: Neem soil drench
remedies.recipe: Cold-pressed neem with a drop of mild soap in water, at label rate.
remedies.how: Water the soil with it once a week for 3 weeks.
remedies.caution: Smells strong. Keep away from fish ponds.

remedies.name: Chamomile tea
remedies.recipe: Cooled weak chamomile tea.
remedies.how: Water seedlings with it or mist trays.
remedies.caution: A gentle home remedy, not a cure.

remedies.name: Small fan
remedies.forWhat: mould, mildew, damping off, leggy seedlings
remedies.recipe: A small fan on low.
remedies.how: Run it a few hours a day near plants.
remedies.caution: Don't blast plants all day.

remedies.name: Humidifier
remedies.forWhat: dry air, crispy tips, spider mites
remedies.recipe: A cool-mist humidifier.
remedies.how: Run it near tropical plants. Aim for 50 to 60%.
remedies.caution: Clean it weekly. Avoid wetting walls.

remedies.name: Pebble tray
remedies.recipe: A tray of pebbles topped with water.
remedies.how: Sit the pot on top, above the water line.
remedies.caution: Helps a little, mainly very close to the plant.

remedies.name: Soil flush
remedies.recipe: Plain water, 3 to 4 times the pot volume.
remedies.how: Pour slowly through the soil and let it drain.
remedies.caution: Let it drain fully; don't leave it in a saucer.

remedies.name: Rainwater
remedies.recipe: Rain collected in a clean butt or bucket.
remedies.how: Use at room temperature for watering.
remedies.caution: Not from roofs with fresh tar or moss killer.

remedies.name: Crushed eggshells
remedies.recipe: Dried, crushed eggshells.
remedies.how: Mix into compost or soil.
remedies.caution: Very slow. Doesn't stop slugs.

remedies.name: Used coffee grounds
remedies.recipe: Used grounds, dried.
remedies.how: Add to compost, not straight onto pots.
remedies.caution: Thick layers mould and repel water.

remedies.name: Banana peel compost
remedies.recipe: Chopped peels.
remedies.how: Compost them first.
remedies.caution: Soaking peels in water attracts flies and adds little.

remedies.name: Tool cleaning
remedies.recipe: 70% alcohol or a 1:10 bleach dilution.
remedies.how: Wipe blades between plants.
remedies.caution: Rinse bleach off to stop rust.

remedies.name: Prune and bin
remedies.recipe: Clean scissors.
remedies.how: Cut off infected leaves and bin them, not compost.
remedies.caution: Don't remove more than a third at once.

remedies.name: Grease band
remedies.recipe: A sticky band around the trunk or pot.
remedies.how: Wrap and check monthly.
remedies.caution: Not directly on young bark.

remedies.name: Insect mesh
remedies.recipe: Fine insect netting.
remedies.how: Cover crops right after sowing or planting.
remedies.caution: Seal edges to the ground.

remedies.name: Bucket soak
remedies.recipe: A bucket of room-temperature water.
remedies.how: Soak the pot for 20 to 30 minutes, then drain.
remedies.caution: Not for succulents in winter.

remedies.name: Fresh repot
remedies.forWhat: root rot, root pests, tired soil
remedies.recipe: Fresh mix and a clean pot.
remedies.how: Shake off old soil, trim bad roots, repot.
remedies.caution: Best in spring.

remedies.name: Bicarbonate spray
remedies.recipe: 1 teaspoon baking soda and a drop of soap in 1 litre water.
remedies.how: Spray weekly on affected leaves.
remedies.caution: Test first. Overuse builds salts in soil.

scenarios.name: Next to a heater in winter
scenarios.advice: Heaters dry the air and the soil fast. Move plants a metre away and raise humidity.

scenarios.name: Cold window in winter
scenarios.advice: Glass gets very cold at night. Pull plants back from the window after dark.

scenarios.name: Watering like summer in winter
scenarios.advice: Plants drink much less in winter. Let the soil dry more between waterings.

scenarios.name: Short dark days
scenarios.advice: Winter light is weak. Move plants closer to the window or add a grow light.

scenarios.name: Near a front door in winter
scenarios.advice: Cold blasts from doors shock tropical plants. Move them somewhere steadier.

scenarios.name: Very dry air in winter
scenarios.advice: Heating can drop humidity under 30%. Group plants or run a humidifier.

scenarios.name: Feeding in winter
scenarios.advice: Resting plants can't use much food. Pause feeding until spring.

scenarios.name: Succulents watered in winter
scenarios.advice: Cold plus wet soil rots succulents. Keep them almost dry until spring.

scenarios.name: Warm, dry flat in winter
scenarios.advice: Mites thrive in warm, dry rooms. Shower plants and check leaf undersides weekly.

scenarios.name: Fungus gnats in winter
scenarios.advice: Slow-drying winter soil breeds gnats. Let the top dry fully between waterings.

scenarios.name: Citrus indoors in winter
scenarios.advice: Citrus wants a bright, cool spot in winter. Keep it away from heaters.

scenarios.name: Christmas plants
scenarios.advice: Holiday plants often get chilled on the way home. Keep them warm and bright.

scenarios.name: Repotted in spring
scenarios.advice: Some droop after repotting is normal. Keep it out of hot sun and water lightly.

scenarios.name: Spring growth
scenarios.advice: New growth attracts aphids and needs more water and food.

scenarios.name: First warm spring sun
scenarios.advice: Spring sun burns plants that wintered in shade. Adapt them over two weeks.

scenarios.name: Starting seeds in spring
scenarios.advice: Seedlings need strong light and airflow. Use a grow light and a small fan.

scenarios.name: Plants out too early
scenarios.advice: Late frosts hit tender plants. Wait until nights stay above 10 °C.

scenarios.name: No feeding since autumn
scenarios.advice: Plants waking up need food. Start feeding at half strength.

scenarios.name: Spring on the balcony
scenarios.advice: Pests wake up with the plants. Check new shoots twice a week.

scenarios.name: Heatwave
scenarios.advice: Water early in the morning and give afternoon shade.

scenarios.name: South window in summer
scenarios.advice: Midday sun through glass can scorch. Add a sheer curtain or move back a little.

scenarios.name: Air-conditioned room
scenarios.advice: Air conditioning dries the air. Keep plants out of the direct flow.

scenarios.name: Hot summer and thrips
scenarios.advice: Thrips boom in heat. Check flowers and new leaves weekly.

scenarios.name: Hot dry summer
scenarios.advice: Dry heat favours mites. Rinse plants weekly.

scenarios.name: Hot humid summer
scenarios.advice: Humid heat favours fungus. Space plants and water in the morning.

scenarios.name: Away in summer
scenarios.advice: Plants dry fast in summer. Soak them before you go and move them out of the sun.

scenarios.name: Balcony in summer
scenarios.advice: Balcony pots heat up fast. Water daily and shade dark pots.

scenarios.name: Tomatoes in summer
scenarios.advice: Water tomatoes steadily every day and feed weekly once fruit sets.

scenarios.name: Herbs in hot weather
scenarios.advice: Heat makes herbs flower. Pinch buds and sow again in cooler weeks.

scenarios.name: Summer storm
scenarios.advice: Move pots to shelter and stake tall plants before storms.

scenarios.name: Bringing plants back inside
scenarios.advice: Inspect and rinse plants before they come in. Some leaf drop is normal.

scenarios.name: Cool autumn nights outdoors
scenarios.advice: Bring tropical plants in before nights fall below 10 °C.

scenarios.name: Wet autumn
scenarios.advice: Raise pots on feet and remove fallen leaves.

scenarios.name: Orchid in autumn
scenarios.advice: A few cooler nights now trigger orchid flower spikes.

scenarios.name: Still feeding in autumn
scenarios.advice: Wind down feeding as growth slows.

scenarios.name: Light fading in autumn
scenarios.advice: Move sun lovers closer to the window as days shorten.

scenarios.name: Frost forecast
scenarios.advice: Bring tender pots in or wrap them in fleece overnight.

scenarios.name: Cold snap with cold rooms
scenarios.advice: Keep plants off cold sills and away from draughts until it warms.

scenarios.name: Week of rain
scenarios.advice: Move succulents under cover and empty saucers.

scenarios.name: Muggy weather indoors
scenarios.advice: Open windows and let soil dry before watering.

scenarios.name: Dry, windy weather
scenarios.advice: Water more often and give wind shelter.

scenarios.name: Weeks of cloudy days
scenarios.advice: Less light means slower drying. Water less and move plants closer to light.

scenarios.name: Windy high balcony
scenarios.advice: Use heavy pots, a windbreak and tough plants.

scenarios.name: Storm coming
scenarios.advice: Lay tall pots down or move them to a sheltered wall.

scenarios.name: Very warm room
scenarios.advice: Warm rooms dry plants fast. Check soil more often.

scenarios.name: Cold room
scenarios.advice: Most houseplants want at least 15 °C. Water less in cold rooms.

scenarios.name: Very dry air
scenarios.advice: Group plants, use a humidifier and keep away from heaters.

scenarios.name: Very humid air
scenarios.advice: Humid, still air invites fungus. Add airflow.

scenarios.name: Dark room
scenarios.advice: Most plants struggle without daylight. Use a grow light or choose tough plants.

scenarios.name: North-facing window
scenarios.advice: Soft light suits ferns and calatheas, not sun lovers.

scenarios.name: South-facing window
scenarios.advice: Great for sun lovers. Shade tender leaves in summer.

scenarios.name: In the bathroom
scenarios.advice: Steam suits ferns. Ventilate after showers and check the light is enough.

scenarios.name: In the kitchen
scenarios.advice: Keep plants away from the hob and fruit bowl. Wipe greasy leaves.

scenarios.name: In an office
scenarios.advice: Water deeply before weekends and use a desk lamp if it's dim.

scenarios.name: Grow light too close
scenarios.advice: Raise the light to 20 to 40 cm above leaves.

scenarios.name: Grow light too far
scenarios.advice: Lower the light; it loses strength fast with distance.

scenarios.name: On a balcony
scenarios.advice: Balconies are sunnier and windier than they look. Water and check often.

scenarios.name: In the garden
scenarios.advice: Outdoor plants meet more pests. Check them twice a week.

scenarios.name: Terracotta pot
scenarios.advice: Clay dries fast. Great for succulents; water thirsty plants more often.

scenarios.name: Plastic pot
scenarios.advice: Plastic holds moisture. Check before watering again.

scenarios.name: Pot without holes
scenarios.advice: Water pools at the bottom. Use a nursery pot with holes inside it.

scenarios.name: Self-watering pot
scenarios.advice: Let the reservoir run dry for a few days between fills.

scenarios.name: Pot much too big
scenarios.advice: Extra soil stays wet. Move to a pot just bigger than the roots.

scenarios.name: Pot too small
scenarios.advice: Repot one size up in spring.

scenarios.name: Wilting right after watering
scenarios.advice: Wilting with wet soil points to the roots. Check them.

scenarios.name: Not watered for weeks
scenarios.advice: Soak the pot in water for 30 minutes, then drain.

scenarios.name: Garden clay in pots
scenarios.advice: Garden clay is too heavy for pots. Repot in a proper potting mix.

scenarios.name: Peat mix dried out
scenarios.advice: Dry peat repels water. Soak the pot from below.

scenarios.name: Acid lovers in chalky soil
scenarios.advice: Chalk locks up iron. Use ericaceous mix and rainwater.

scenarios.name: Sandy soil
scenarios.advice: Sand loses water and food. Mulch and feed little and often.

scenarios.name: Coir without feed
scenarios.advice: Coir holds little food. Feed regularly, with calcium and magnesium.

scenarios.name: LECA reservoir too high
scenarios.advice: Keep the water line below the roots and flush weekly.

scenarios.name: Old sphagnum
scenarios.advice: Old moss turns slimy. Replace it yearly.

scenarios.name: Gritty mix in summer
scenarios.advice: Gritty mixes dry fast in summer. Water deeply when dry.

scenarios.name: Succulent in regular soil
scenarios.advice: Regular mix stays too wet. Repot in cactus mix.

scenarios.name: Just repotted
scenarios.advice: Give it shade and two weeks of calm. Don't feed for a month.

scenarios.name: Just moved to a new spot
scenarios.advice: Plants dislike change. Leave it in place and give it time.

scenarios.name: New plant from the shop
scenarios.advice: Quarantine for two weeks and check for pests.

scenarios.name: Back from holiday
scenarios.advice: Soak thirsty pots from below and trim crisp leaves.

scenarios.name: Taking cuttings
scenarios.advice: Keep cuttings warm and bright, and change water often.

scenarios.name: Just fertilised
scenarios.advice: Too strong a feed burns roots. Flush if leaves brown suddenly.

scenarios.name: Moved outside
scenarios.advice: Start in shade and give more sun slowly.

scenarios.name: Moved inside
scenarios.advice: Indoor light is far weaker. Give the brightest spot.

scenarios.name: Moving house
scenarios.advice: Keep plants warm in the car and unpack them first.

scenarios.name: Tropical plant in a cool flat
scenarios.advice: Tropicals want 18 °C or more and humid air.

scenarios.name: Outdoors in a humid tropical climate
scenarios.advice: Use airy mixes and remove spotted leaves fast.

scenarios.name: Dry, hot climate
scenarios.advice: Shade at midday and water deeply but often.

scenarios.name: Dry Mediterranean summer
scenarios.advice: Water early and mulch pots.

scenarios.name: Pots outdoors in a cold winter
scenarios.advice: Wrap pots and move them against a house wall.

scenarios.name: Terracotta pot by a heater
scenarios.advice: Clay and heat dry soil in days. Check it twice a week.

scenarios.name: Self-watering pot in winter
scenarios.advice: Fill the reservoir less often in winter.

scenarios.name: Oversized pot in winter
scenarios.advice: Big pots stay wet all winter. Water small amounts.

scenarios.name: Repotted in winter
scenarios.advice: Roots grow slowly in winter. Keep watering light until spring.

scenarios.name: New plant bought in winter
scenarios.advice: Shops and cars can chill plants. Wrap them for the trip home.

scenarios.name: Away over winter holidays
scenarios.advice: Leave the heating on low and water before you go.

scenarios.name: Cuttings in winter
scenarios.advice: Rooting is slow in winter. Use a warm spot or wait for spring.

scenarios.name: Bathroom in winter
scenarios.advice: Unheated bathrooms get cold. Move tropicals somewhere warmer.

scenarios.name: Office closed over winter break
scenarios.advice: Offices cool down during breaks. Take tender plants home.

scenarios.name: Grow light in winter
scenarios.advice: Lights add warmth and light, so pots dry faster.

scenarios.name: Balcony in winter
scenarios.advice: Hardy pots still need a drink on mild days. Bring tender ones in.

scenarios.name: Sunny window in winter
scenarios.advice: Great winter light. Pull plants back from the glass at night.

scenarios.name: Ferns in winter heating
scenarios.advice: Ferns hate dry heat. Move them to a cooler, humid room.

scenarios.name: Calathea in winter
scenarios.advice: Keep calatheas warm, humid and evenly moist.

scenarios.name: Alocasia in winter
scenarios.advice: Alocasias may rest. Water lightly and wait for spring.

scenarios.name: Orchid on a winter sill
scenarios.advice: Keep orchids off cold glass, but in good light.

scenarios.name: Fiddle leaf fig in winter
scenarios.advice: Water less and give it the brightest spot.

scenarios.name: Herbs on a winter sill
scenarios.advice: Winter herbs grow slowly. A grow light keeps them going.

scenarios.name: Repotted into terracotta
scenarios.advice: Clay dries faster than plastic. Water more often.

scenarios.name: Repotted into a much bigger pot
scenarios.advice: Go up only one size. Water small amounts until roots fill it.

scenarios.name: Feeding again in spring
scenarios.advice: Start at half strength on moist soil.

scenarios.name: Plants moved out in spring
scenarios.advice: Harden off over two weeks.

scenarios.name: Rainy spring
scenarios.advice: Check for slugs at night and clear fallen leaves.

scenarios.name: Spring cold snap
scenarios.advice: Cover or bring in young plants for the night.

scenarios.name: Spring garden centre buy
scenarios.advice: Check under leaves and in the soil before planting.

scenarios.name: Cuttings in spring
scenarios.advice: Spring is the best time for cuttings. Keep them bright and warm.

scenarios.name: Orchid in bloom in spring
scenarios.advice: Don't move orchids while in bud.

scenarios.name: Bulbs after flowering
scenarios.advice: Let the leaves die back naturally to feed next year's flowers.

scenarios.name: Citrus going out in spring
scenarios.advice: Start in light shade, then full sun.

scenarios.name: Terracotta in summer
scenarios.advice: Clay pots may need daily water in heat.

scenarios.name: Small pot in summer
scenarios.advice: Small pots dry in hours. Repot or water daily.

scenarios.name: Self-watering pot in summer
scenarios.advice: Flush the soil from the top now and then.

scenarios.name: Pot without holes in summer
scenarios.advice: Rain fills holeless pots. Tip them or drill a hole.

scenarios.name: Repotted in summer heat
scenarios.advice: Keep fresh repots in shade until they settle.

scenarios.name: Moved into summer sun
scenarios.advice: Move into sun slowly over two weeks.

scenarios.name: New plant in summer
scenarios.advice: Pests travel in summer. Quarantine new plants.

scenarios.name: Cuttings in summer
scenarios.advice: Change water often; warm water rots stems.

scenarios.name: Feeding in summer heat
scenarios.advice: Feed on moist soil, never on dry, stressed plants.

scenarios.name: Bathroom in summer
scenarios.advice: Ventilate well to stop mould.

scenarios.name: Kitchen in summer
scenarios.advice: Keep herbs out of hot spots and fruit bowls tidy.

scenarios.name: Office in summer
scenarios.advice: Office cooling dries plants. Water before weekends.

scenarios.name: Dark room in summer
scenarios.advice: Summer is the time to give dim plants a brighter spot.

scenarios.name: Grow light in summer
scenarios.advice: Raise the lamp or shorten its hours in heat.

scenarios.name: Monsoon season
scenarios.advice: Shelter pots from constant rain and improve drainage.

scenarios.name: Cool, cloudy summer
scenarios.advice: Water in the morning and give airflow.

scenarios.name: Roses in summer
scenarios.advice: Clear spotted leaves and water at the base.

scenarios.name: Garden pests in summer
scenarios.advice: Check plants at dusk and cover crops with mesh.

scenarios.name: Strawberries in summer
scenarios.advice: Net berries and lift fruit off wet soil.

scenarios.name: Peppers in a heatwave
scenarios.advice: Shade at midday and water evenly.

scenarios.name: Succulents outside in summer
scenarios.advice: Adapt to full sun slowly; then they love it.

scenarios.name: Cacti in summer rain
scenarios.advice: Move cacti under cover in long rain.

scenarios.name: Repotted in autumn
scenarios.advice: Roots slow down in autumn. Water lightly.

scenarios.name: New plant in autumn
scenarios.advice: Shorter days make new plants slow to settle.

scenarios.name: Away in autumn
scenarios.advice: Plants drink less now; a deep soak before you go is enough.

scenarios.name: Autumn storms
scenarios.advice: Move pots against walls and stake tall plants.

scenarios.name: Damp autumn
scenarios.advice: Remove infected leaves and give airflow.

scenarios.name: Heating switched on
scenarios.advice: The first heating weeks shock plants. Raise humidity.

scenarios.name: Gnats in autumn
scenarios.advice: Cooler soil stays wet longer. Water less.

scenarios.name: Poinsettia dark treatment
scenarios.advice: Give 14 hours of total darkness nightly from October.

scenarios.name: Christmas cactus buds
scenarios.advice: Cool nights bring buds. Don't move it once they form.

scenarios.name: Clay pot near a radiator
scenarios.advice: Move it away or switch to a plastic inner pot.

scenarios.name: Succulent by a radiator
scenarios.advice: Warm and dim makes succulents stretch. Give more light.

scenarios.name: Calathea in air conditioning
scenarios.advice: Move it out of the airflow and raise humidity.

scenarios.name: Tropicals near air conditioning
scenarios.advice: Cold air from units chills leaves. Move them away.

scenarios.name: Draughty window
scenarios.advice: Seal gaps or move plants into a steady spot.

scenarios.name: Fiddle leaf fig near a door
scenarios.advice: Figs hate draughts. Find a still, bright spot.

scenarios.name: Succulent in a north window
scenarios.advice: Succulents need much more light. Move them to the sunniest window.

scenarios.name: Fern in a north window
scenarios.advice: Ferns enjoy soft light. Just keep them moist.

scenarios.name: Calathea in a sunny window
scenarios.advice: Move calatheas out of direct sun.

scenarios.name: Fern in hot sun
scenarios.advice: Ferns scorch in sun. Move to bright shade.

scenarios.name: Cactus in a sunny window
scenarios.advice: Ideal spot. Turn it so all sides get light.

scenarios.name: Variegated plant in low light
scenarios.advice: Variegated leaves need more light than plain ones.

scenarios.name: Succulent in a dark room
scenarios.advice: Succulents can't live in low light. Move them to a sunny window.

scenarios.name: Monstera in a dim spot
scenarios.advice: More light brings bigger, split leaves.

scenarios.name: Pothos in a dim spot
scenarios.advice: Pothos survives shade but grows small leaves. Move it brighter.

scenarios.name: Snake plant in a dim spot
scenarios.advice: Low light slows drying. Water rarely.

scenarios.name: Orchid in the bathroom
scenarios.advice: Humidity helps, but keep water out of the crown.

scenarios.name: Fern in the bathroom
scenarios.advice: Ferns love bathrooms with a window.

scenarios.name: Windowless bathroom
scenarios.advice: No window means no growth. Add a grow light or rotate plants.

scenarios.name: Herbs on the kitchen sill
scenarios.advice: Pinch herbs often and check under leaves.

scenarios.name: Flowers near the fruit bowl
scenarios.advice: Ripening fruit releases ethylene. Keep flowers away from it.

scenarios.name: Office plants over the weekend
scenarios.advice: Water deeply on Friday.

scenarios.name: Office under ceiling lights
scenarios.advice: Ceiling lights are weak. Use a desk grow light.

scenarios.name: Birds on the balcony
scenarios.advice: Net seedlings and cover soil with stones.

scenarios.name: Squirrels digging pots
scenarios.advice: Cover pots with wire mesh.

scenarios.name: Cats in the pots
scenarios.advice: Cover soil with stones and give cats their own grass.

scenarios.name: Wet nights in the garden
scenarios.advice: Check at night with a torch and remove them.

scenarios.name: Ants in garden pots
scenarios.advice: Ants farm aphids. Treat the aphids and flood the pot.

scenarios.name: Vegetable patch
scenarios.advice: Rotate crops and cover with mesh.

scenarios.name: Roses in the garden
scenarios.advice: Clear fallen leaves and give airflow.

scenarios.name: Lilies in the garden
scenarios.advice: Pick off red beetles as soon as you see them.

scenarios.name: Fruit trees
scenarios.advice: Prune for airflow and remove rotten fruit.

scenarios.name: Box hedges
scenarios.advice: Check inside the hedge for webbing in spring and summer.

scenarios.name: Succulent in terracotta
scenarios.advice: A perfect match. Water deeply when fully dry.

scenarios.name: Fern in terracotta
scenarios.advice: Clay dries ferns fast. Use plastic or water more often.

scenarios.name: Succulent in plastic
scenarios.advice: Plastic stays wet. Water less or switch to clay.

scenarios.name: Succulent in a pot with no hole
scenarios.advice: Succulents need drainage. Repot into a pot with holes.

scenarios.name: Orchid in a self-watering pot
scenarios.advice: Orchid roots need air. Use bark in a clear pot instead.

scenarios.name: Succulent in a big pot
scenarios.advice: Use a snug pot for succulents.

scenarios.name: Monstera in a small pot
scenarios.advice: Repot one size up in spring and add support.

scenarios.name: Tomato in a small pot
scenarios.advice: Tomatoes need at least 20 litres.

scenarios.name: Watering every few days
scenarios.advice: Wait for the top of the soil to dry.

scenarios.name: Yellowing after a big watering
scenarios.advice: Tip out any water sitting in the pot.

scenarios.name: Peace lily not watered
scenarios.advice: It will perk up within hours of a good drink.

scenarios.name: Succulent left dry for months
scenarios.advice: Water deeply; it should plump up in days.

scenarios.name: Fern left dry
scenarios.advice: Ferns rarely recover crisp fronds. Cut them off and keep it moist.

scenarios.name: Soil bone dry for weeks
scenarios.advice: Soak the pot in a bucket so water can soak in.

scenarios.name: Chunky aroid mix
scenarios.advice: Chunky mixes dry faster. Water a little more often.

scenarios.name: Orchid bark
scenarios.advice: Bark breaks down in 2 years. Repot then.

scenarios.name: Ericaceous mix
scenarios.advice: Use rainwater to keep acid mixes acid.

scenarios.name: Seed mix
scenarios.advice: Keep the surface just moist and give airflow.

scenarios.name: Cutting mix
scenarios.advice: Keep it lightly moist, not soggy.

scenarios.name: Rich container mix
scenarios.advice: Water evenly and feed weekly once fruits form.

scenarios.name: Bog mix
scenarios.advice: Keep it wet with rainwater only.

scenarios.name: Garden soil in a pot
scenarios.advice: Garden soil packs down in pots. Mix with compost and grit.

scenarios.name: Volcanic or lava mix
scenarios.advice: Mineral mixes hold little food. Feed lightly and often.

scenarios.name: Bonsai in akadama
scenarios.advice: Small bonsai pots dry fast. Check daily in summer.

scenarios.name: Unrinsed coir
scenarios.advice: Rinse coir before use to remove salt.

scenarios.name: Closed terrarium
scenarios.advice: Air it out for a few days if it fogs.

scenarios.name: Repotted into a pot without holes
scenarios.advice: Drill a hole or use an inner pot.

scenarios.name: Moved to a darker spot
scenarios.advice: Move it back toward the light.

scenarios.name: Moved to a brighter spot
scenarios.advice: Brighter spots need slow adjustment.

scenarios.name: New plant brought gnats
scenarios.advice: Let the soil dry and use yellow traps.

scenarios.name: New plant with white fluff
scenarios.advice: Isolate it and check leaf joints.

scenarios.name: Plant sitter overwatered
scenarios.advice: Let the soil dry well before watering again.

scenarios.name: Away during a heatwave
scenarios.advice: Move plants out of sun and use wicks before leaving.

scenarios.name: Rooting in water
scenarios.advice: Change the water twice a week and use an opaque jar.

scenarios.name: Succulent leaf propagation
scenarios.advice: Keep leaves in bright shade, not full sun.

scenarios.name: Fed on dry soil
scenarios.advice: Water first, then feed.

scenarios.name: Feed too strong
scenarios.advice: Flush the pot and use half strength next time.

scenarios.name: Leafy but no flowers after feeding
scenarios.advice: Too much nitrogen gives leaves, not flowers. Switch to a bloom feed.

scenarios.name: Cold and damp
scenarios.advice: Water less and add warmth and airflow.

scenarios.name: Hot and humid
scenarios.advice: Space plants and avoid wetting leaves.

scenarios.name: Hot and dry
scenarios.advice: Raise humidity and water more often.

scenarios.name: Cold and dry
scenarios.advice: Keep plants away from windows and heaters alike.

scenarios.name: Bright and dry
scenarios.advice: Group plants and shade at midday.

scenarios.name: Dim and overwatered
scenarios.advice: Low light means slow drying. Water much less.

scenarios.name: Flowering plant in low light
scenarios.advice: Flowers need light. Move it to a bright window.

scenarios.name: Plants in a hot car
scenarios.advice: Never leave plants in a parked car in sun.

scenarios.name: Plant arrived by post
scenarios.advice: Unpack at once, water if dry, and keep it out of sun for a few days.

scenarios.name: Plant shipped in winter
scenarios.advice: Unpack somewhere warm and trim damaged leaves later.

scenarios.name: Moving house in winter
scenarios.advice: Wrap plants and keep them in the warm car.

scenarios.name: Moving house in summer
scenarios.advice: Water before the move and keep plants out of the hot van.

scenarios.name: New home with different light
scenarios.advice: Watch plants for a few weeks and adjust their spots.

scenarios.name: Plants in an unheated room
scenarios.advice: Water very little in cold rooms.

scenarios.name: Conservatory
scenarios.advice: Ventilate and shade in summer.

scenarios.name: Greenhouse
scenarios.advice: Open vents daily and hang sticky traps.

scenarios.name: Plants behind curtains at night
scenarios.advice: Curtains trap plants against cold glass. Move them inside the room.

scenarios.name: Under a skylight
scenarios.advice: Overhead sun is strong. Shade it in summer.

scenarios.name: Basement flat
scenarios.advice: Use grow lights and keep soil on the dry side.

scenarios.name: Small, warm room
scenarios.advice: Choose tough plants and water regularly.

scenarios.name: LECA in summer
scenarios.advice: Warm water holds less oxygen. Refresh it more often.

scenarios.name: New to semi-hydro
scenarios.advice: Some old roots die during the switch. New water roots will grow.

scenarios.name: Herbs in a rainy spell
scenarios.advice: Shelter basil and water only at the base.

scenarios.name: Mint in damp shade
scenarios.advice: Give mint more light and airflow.

scenarios.name: Tomatoes in wet weather
scenarios.advice: Remove lower leaves and shelter if you can.

scenarios.name: Tomatoes on cool nights
scenarios.advice: Tomatoes stall below 10 °C. Wait for warmer weather.

scenarios.name: Citrus with hard tap water
scenarios.advice: Use rainwater and a citrus feed with iron.

scenarios.name: Orchid with weak light
scenarios.advice: Move it to an east window for blooms.

scenarios.name: Orchid watered weekly by habit
scenarios.advice: Water only when roots look silver.

scenarios.name: Succulents under grow lights
scenarios.advice: Keep lights close and on for 12 to 14 hours.

scenarios.name: Cactus outdoors in summer
scenarios.advice: Adapt to sun slowly and check for mealybugs.

scenarios.name: Fiddle leaf fig moved
scenarios.advice: Leave it in the new spot; it will settle in weeks.

scenarios.name: Monstera without support
scenarios.advice: Add a moss pole when you next repot.

scenarios.name: Pothos in a pot without holes
scenarios.advice: Use an inner pot with holes.

scenarios.name: Snake plant watered in winter
scenarios.advice: Water once a month or less in winter.

scenarios.name: ZZ plant watered often
scenarios.advice: ZZ stores water. Let it dry completely.

scenarios.name: Peace lily with tap water
scenarios.advice: Use filtered water or let tap water stand overnight.

scenarios.name: Dracaena with fluoride water
scenarios.advice: Use filtered water.

scenarios.name: Spider plant with tap water
scenarios.advice: Filtered or rainwater keeps tips green.

scenarios.name: Carnivorous plant with tap water
scenarios.advice: Use only rain or distilled water.

scenarios.name: Air plant stays wet
scenarios.advice: Dry air plants upside down after soaking.

scenarios.name: Bromeliad in a cold room
scenarios.advice: Empty the cup in cold weather.

scenarios.name: Alocasia in dry air
scenarios.advice: Check undersides often and raise humidity.

scenarios.name: Hoya moved while budding
scenarios.advice: Leave budding hoyas where they are.

scenarios.name: Outdoor bonsai kept indoors
scenarios.advice: Most bonsai need a cold winter outside.

scenarios.name: Ivy by a heater
scenarios.advice: Ivy likes it cool. Move it away from heat.

scenarios.name: Tradescantia in low light
scenarios.advice: More light keeps it colourful and full.

scenarios.name: Seeds in a cold room
scenarios.advice: Use a heat mat or a warm spot.

scenarios.name: Seedlings with no grow light
scenarios.advice: Seedlings need strong light from day one.

scenarios.name: Microgreens going mouldy
scenarios.advice: Water from below and give a fan breeze.

scenarios.name: Strawberries in shade
scenarios.advice: Strawberries need 6 hours of sun.

scenarios.name: Lettuce in summer heat
scenarios.advice: Grow lettuce in light shade and sow small batches.

scenarios.name: Cabbage family in acid soil
scenarios.advice: Lime the soil and rotate crops.

scenarios.name: Blueberries in alkaline soil
scenarios.advice: Grow blueberries in pots of ericaceous mix.

scenarios.name: Pond and bog plants
scenarios.advice: Keep water topped up with rainwater.

scenarios.name: Raised bed in summer
scenarios.advice: Raised beds drain fast. Mulch and water deeply.

scenarios.name: Mediterranean herbs in rich soil
scenarios.advice: Herbs like lean, gritty soil.

scenarios.name: Coir without calcium
scenarios.advice: Add a calcium and magnesium supplement.

scenarios.name: Hard water over years
scenarios.advice: Repot in fresh mix and switch to rain or filtered water.

scenarios.name: Feeding into a self-watering reservoir
scenarios.advice: Flush the soil from the top every month.

scenarios.name: Bulbs in pots outdoors
scenarios.advice: Cover pots with mesh until shoots appear.

scenarios.name: Plants in a cold frame
scenarios.advice: Open the lid on sunny days.

scenarios.name: Condensation on windows
scenarios.advice: Wipe windows and give a little airflow.

scenarios.name: Humidifier running all day
scenarios.advice: Aim for 50 to 60%, not more.

scenarios.name: Fan blowing on plants
scenarios.advice: A gentle, indirect breeze is enough.

scenarios.name: Pets chewing plants
scenarios.advice: Move plants up high and check they are pet-safe.

scenarios.name: Plants knocked about
scenarios.advice: Place delicate plants out of busy spots.

scenarios.name: Away for a month
scenarios.advice: For long trips, use wicks, group plants and ask someone to check.

scenarios.name: Away for a weekend
scenarios.advice: Most plants are fine. Water thirsty ones before you go.

scenarios.name: Plant sitter forgot
scenarios.advice: Soak from below, trim crisp parts and give it time.

scenarios.name: Rainforest plants in a dry flat
scenarios.advice: Group them with a humidifier.

scenarios.name: Desert plants in a humid home
scenarios.advice: Give them the sunniest, airiest spot and water less.

scenarios.name: Coastal salty wind
scenarios.advice: Choose salt-tolerant plants and rinse leaves after storms.

scenarios.name: Busy city balcony
scenarios.advice: Rinse leaves monthly.

scenarios.name: High altitude
scenarios.advice: Strong UV and dry air: shade and water more.

scenarios.name: Hail storm
scenarios.advice: Trim shredded leaves once it settles.

scenarios.name: Snow on outdoor pots
scenarios.advice: Brush heavy snow off branches gently.

scenarios.name: Heating off in winter
scenarios.advice: Group plants away from windows and cover them overnight.

scenarios.name: Grow tent
scenarios.advice: Run a small fan and open the tent daily.

scenarios.name: Radiator under the windowsill
scenarios.advice: Put a board under the pots or move them.

scenarios.name: East-facing window
scenarios.advice: Gentle morning sun suits most houseplants.
